entries.label: II
entries.original: CONCERNING THE POSTERITY OF ADAM, AND THE TEN GENERATIONS FROM HIM TO THE DELUGE.
entries.display: Concerning the posterity of Adam, and the ten generations from him to the deluge.

entries.label: III
entries.original: CONCERNING THE FLOOD; AND AFTER WHAT MANNER NOAH WAS SAVED IN AN ARK, WITH HIS KINDRED, AND AFTERWARDS DWELT IN THE PLAIN OF SHINAR.
entries.display: Concerning the flood; and after what manner Noah was saved in an ark, with his kindred, and afterwards dwelt in the plain of Shinar.

entries.label: IV
entries.original: CONCERNING THE TOWER OF BABYLON, AND THE CONFUSION OF TONGUES.
entries.display: Concerning the tower of Babylon, and the confusion of tongues.

entries.label: V
entries.original: AFTER WHAT MANNER THE POSTERITY OF NOAH SENT OUT COLONIES, AND INHABITED THE WHOLE EARTH.
entries.display: After what manner the posterity of Noah sent out colonies, and inhabited the whole earth.

entries.label: VI
entries.original: HOW EVERY NATION WAS DENOMINATED FROM THEIR FIRST INHABITANTS.
entries.display: How every nation was denominated from their first inhabitants.

entries.label: VII
entries.original: HOW ABRAM OUR FOREFATHER WENT OUT OF THE LAND OF THE CHALDEANS, AND LIVED IN THE LAND THEN CALLED CANAAN, BUT NOW JUDEA.
entries.display: How Abram our forefather went out of the land of the Chaldeans, and lived in the land then called Canaan, but now Judea.

entries.label: VIII
entries.original: THAT WHEN THERE WAS A FAMINE IN CANAAN ABRAM WENT THENCE INTO EGYPT; AND AFTER HE HAD CONTINUED THERE A WHILE, HE RETURNED BACK AGAIN.
entries.display: That when there was a famine in Canaan Abram went thence into Egypt; and after he had continued there a while, he returned back again.

entries.label: IX
entries.original: THE DESTRUCTION OF THE SODOMITES BY THE ASSYRIAN WAR.
entries.display: The destruction of the Sodomites by the Assyrian war.

entries.label: X
entries.original: HOW ABRAM FOUGHT WITH THE ASSYRIANS, AND OVERCAME THEM, AND SAVED THE SODOMITE PRISONERS, AND TOOK FROM THE ASSYRIANS THE PREY THEY HAD GOTTEN.
entries.display: How Abram fought with the Assyrians, and overcame them, and saved the Sodomite prisoners, and took from the Assyrians the prey they had gotten.

entries.label: XI
entries.original: HOW GOD OVERTHREW THE NATION OF THE SODOMITES, OUT OF HIS WRATH AGAINST THEM FOR THEIR SINS.
entries.display: How God overthrew the nation of the Sodomites, out of his wrath against them for their sins.

entries.label: XII
entries.original: CONCERNING ABIMELECH; AND CONCERNING ISMAEL, THE SON OF ABRAHAM; AND CONCERNING THE ARABIANS, WHO WERE HIS POSTERITY.
entries.display: Concerning Abimelech; and concerning Ismael, the son of Abraham; and concerning the Arabians, who were his posterity.

entries.label: XIII
entries.original: CONCERNING ISAAC, THE LEGITIMATE SON OF ABRAHAM.
entries.display: Concerning Isaac, the legitimate son of Abraham.

entries.label: XIV
entries.original: CONCERNING SARAH, ABRAHAM'S WIFE: AND HOW SHE ENDED HER DAYS.
entries.display: Concerning Sarah, Abraham's wife: and how she ended her days.

entries.label: XV
entries.original: HOW THE NATION OF THE TROGLODYTES WERE DERIVED FROM ABRAHAM BY KETURAH.
entries.display: How the nation of the Troglodytes were derived from Abraham by Keturah.

entries.label: XVI
entries.original: HOW ISAAC TOOK REBEKA TO WIFE.
entries.display: How Isaac took Rebeka to wife.

entries.label: XVII
entries.original: CONCERNING THE DEATH OF ABRAHAM.
entries.display: Concerning the death of Abraham.

entries.label: XVIII
entries.original: CONCERNING THE SONS OF ISAAC, ESAU AND JACOB, OF THEIR NATIVITY AND EDUCATION.
entries.display: Concerning the sons of Isaac, Esau and Jacob, of their nativity and education.

entries.label: XIX
entries.original: CONCERNING JACOB'S FLIGHT INTO MESOPOTAMIA, BY REASON OF THE FEAR HE WAS IN OF HIS BROTHER.
entries.display: Concerning Jacob's flight into Mesopotamia, by reason of the fear he was in of his brother.

entries.label: XX
entries.original: CONCERNING THE MEETING OF JACOB AND ESAU.
entries.display: Concerning the meeting of Jacob and Esau.

entries.label: XXI
entries.original: CONCERNING THE VIOLATION OF DINA'S CHASTITY.
entries.display: Concerning the violation of Dina's chastity.

entries.label: XXII
entries.original: HOW ISAAC DIED, AND WAS BURIED IN HEBRON.
entries.display: How Isaac died, and was buried in Hebron.

entries.label: I
entries.original: HOW ESAU AND JACOB, ISAAC'S SONS, DIVIDED THEIR HABITATION; AND ESAU POSSESSED IDUMEA, AND JACOB CANAAN.
entries.display: How Esau and Jacob, Isaac's sons, divided their habitation; and Esau possessed Idumea, and Jacob Canaan.

entries.label: II
entries.original: HOW JOSEPH, THE YOUNGEST OF JACOB'S SONS, WAS ENVIED BY HIS BRETHREN, WHEN CERTAIN DREAMS HAD FORESHOWN HIS FUTURE HAPPINESS.
entries.display: How Joseph, the youngest of Jacob's sons, was envied by his brethren, when certain dreams had foreshown his future happiness.

entries.label: III
entries.original: HOW JOSEPH WAS THUS SOLD BY HIS BRETHREN INTO EGYPT, BY REASON OF THEIR HATRED TO HIM; AND HOW HE THERE GREW FAMOUS AND ILLUSTRIOUS, AND HAD HIS BRETHREN UNDER HIS POWER.
entries.display: How Joseph was thus sold by his brethren into Egypt, by reason of their hatred to him; and how he there grew famous and illustrious, and had his brethren under his power.

entries.label: IV
entries.original: CONCERNING THE SIGNAL CHASTITY OF JOSEPH.
entries.display: Concerning the signal chastity of Joseph.

entries.label: V
entries.original: WHAT THINGS BEFELL JOSEPH IN PRISON.
entries.display: What things befell Joseph in prison.

entries.label: VI
entries.original: HOW JOSEPH, WHEN HE WAS BECOME FAMOUS IN EGYPT, HAD HIS BRETHREN IN SUBJECTION.
entries.display: How Joseph, when he was become famous in Egypt, had his brethren in subjection.

entries.label: VII
entries.original: THE REMOVAL OF JOSEPH'S FATHER, WITH ALL HIS FAMILY, TO HIM, ON ACCOUNT OF THE FAMINE.
entries.display: The removal of Joseph's father, with all his family, to him, on account of the famine.

entries.label: VIII
entries.original: OF THE DEATH OF JACOB AND JOSEPH.
entries.display: Of the death of Jacob and Joseph.

entries.label: IX
entries.original: CONCERNING THE AFFLICTIONS THAT BEFELL THE HEBREWS IN EGYPT, DURING FOUR HUNDRED YEARS.*
entries.display: Concerning the afflictions that befell the Hebrews in Egypt, during four hundred years.*

entries.label: X
entries.original: HOW MOSES MADE WAR WITH THE ETHIOPIANS.
entries.display: How Moses made war with the Ethiopians.

entries.label: XI
entries.original: HOW MOSES FLED OUT OF EGYPT INTO MIDIAN.
entries.display: How Moses fled out of Egypt into Midian.

entries.label: XII
entries.original: CONCERNING THE BURNING BUSH, AND THE ROD OF MOSES.
entries.display: Concerning the burning bush, and the rod of Moses.

entries.label: XIII
entries.original: HOW MOSES AND AARON RETURNED INTO EGYPT TO PHARAOH.
entries.display: How Moses and Aaron returned into Egypt to Pharaoh.

entries.label: XIV
entries.original: CONCERNING THE TEN PLAGUES WHICH CAME UPON THE EGYPTIANS.
entries.display: Concerning the ten plagues which came upon the Egyptians.

entries.label: XV
entries.original: HOW THE HEBREWS, UNDER THE CONDUCT OF MOSES, LEFT EGYPT.
entries.display: How the Hebrews, under the conduct of Moses, left Egypt.

entries.label: XVI
entries.original: HOW THE SEA WAS DIVIDED ASUNDER FOR THE HEBREWS, WHEN THEY WERE PURSUED BY THE EGYPTIANS, AND SO GAVE THEM AN OPPORTUNITY OF ESCAPING FROM THEM.
entries.display: How the sea was divided asunder for the Hebrews, when they were pursued by the Egyptians, and so gave them an opportunity of escaping from them.

entries.label: I
entries.original: HOW MOSES, WHEN HE HAD BROUGHT THE PEOPLE OUT OF EGYPT, LED THEM TO MOUNT SINAI; BUT NOT TILL THEY HAD SUFFERED MUCH IN THEIR JOURNEY.
entries.display: How Moses, when he had brought the people out of Egypt, led them to Mount Sinai; but not till they had suffered much in their journey.

entries.label: II
entries.original: HOW THE AMALEKITES, AND THE NEIGHBOURING NATIONS, MADE WAR WITH THE HEBREWS, AND WERE BEATEN, AND LOST A GREAT PART OF THEIR ARMY.
entries.display: How the Amalekites, and the neighbouring nations, made war with the Hebrews, and were beaten, and lost a great part of their army.

entries.label: III
entries.original: THAT MOSES KINDLY RECEIVED HIS FATHER-IN-LAW, JETHRO, WHEN HE CAME TO HIM TO MOUNT SINAI.
entries.display: That Moses kindly received his father-in-law, Jethro, when he came to him to Mount Sinai.

entries.label: IV
entries.original: HOW RAGUEL SUGGESTED TO MOSES TO SET HIS PEOPLE IN ORDER, UNDER THEIR RULERS OF THOUSANDS, AND RULERS OF HUNDREDS, WHO LIVED WITHOUT ORDER BEFORE; AND HOW MOSES COMPLIED IN ALL THINGS WITH HIS FATHER-IN-LAW'S ADMONITION.
entries.display: How Raguel suggested to Moses to set his people in order, under their rulers of thousands, and rulers of hundreds, who lived without order before; and how Moses complied in all things with his father-in-law's admonition.

entries.label: V
entries.original: HOW MOSES ASCENDED UP TO MOUNT SINAI, AND RECEIVED LAWS FROM GOD, AND DELIVERED THEM TO THE HEBREWS.
entries.display: How Moses ascended up to Mount Sinai, and received laws from God, and delivered them to the Hebrews.

entries.label: VI
entries.original: CONCERNING THE TABERNACLE WHICH MOSES BUILT IN THE WILDERNESS FOR THE HONOUR OF GOD, AND WHICH SEEMED TO BE A TEMPLE.
entries.display: Concerning the tabernacle which Moses built in the wilderness for the honour of God, and which seemed to be a temple.

entries.label: VII
entries.original: CONCERNING THE GARMENTS OF THE PRIESTS, AND OF THE HIGH-PRIEST.
entries.display: Concerning the garments of the priests, and of the high-priest.

entries.label: VIII
entries.original: OF THE PRIESTHOOD OF AARON
entries.display: Of the priesthood of Aaron

entries.label: IX
entries.original: THE MANNER OF OUR OFFERING SACRIFICES.
entries.display: The manner of our offering sacrifices.

entries.label: X
entries.original: CONCERNING THE FESTIVALS; AND HOW EACH DAY OF SUCH FESTIVAL IS TO BE OBSERVED.
entries.display: Concerning the festivals; and how each day of such festival is to be observed.

entries.label: XI
entries.original: OF THE PURIFICATIONS.
entries.display: Of the purifications.

entries.label: XII
entries.original: SEVERAL LAWS.
entries.display: Several laws.

entries.label: XIII
entries.original: HOW MOSES REMOVED FROM MOUNT SINAI, AND CONDUCTED THE PEOPLE TO THE BORDERS OF THE CANAANITES.
entries.display: How Moses removed from Mount Sinai, and conducted the people to the borders of the Canaanites.

entries.label: XIV
entries.original: HOW MOSES SENT SOME PERSONS TO SEARCH OUT THE LAND OF THE CANAANITES, AND THE LARGENESS OF THEIR CITIES; AND FARTHER, THAT WHEN THOSE WHO WERE SENT WERE RETURNED, AFTER FORTY DAYS, AND REPORTED THAT THEY SHOULD NOT BE A MATCH FOR THEM, AND EXTOLLED THE STRENGTH OF THE CANAANITES, THE MULTITUDE WERE DISTURBED, AND FELL INTO DESPAIR; AND WERE RESOLVED TO STONE MOSES, AND TO RETURN BACK AGAIN INTO EGYPT, AND SERVE THE EGYPTIANS.
entries.display: How Moses sent some persons to search out the land of the Canaanites, and the largeness of their cities; and farther, that when those who were sent were returned, after forty days, and reported that they should not be a match for them, and extolled the strength of the Canaanites, the multitude were disturbed, and fell into despair; and were resolved to stone Moses, and to return back again into Egypt, and serve the Egyptians.

entries.label: XV
entries.original: HOW MOSES WAS DISPLEASED AT THIS, AND FORETOLD THAT GOD WAS ANGRY, AND THAT THEY SHOULD CONTINUE IN THE WILDERNESS FOR FORTY YEARS, AND NOT, DURING THAT TIME, EITHER RETURN INTO EGYPT, OR TAKE POSSESSION OF CANAAN.
entries.display: How Moses was displeased at this, and foretold that God was angry, and that they should continue in the wilderness for forty years, and not, during that time, either return into Egypt, or take possession of Canaan.

entries.label: I
entries.original: THE FIGHT OF THE HEBREWS WITH THE CANAANITES, WITHOUT THE CONSENT OF MOSES; AND THEIR DEFEAT.
entries.display: The fight of the Hebrews with the Canaanites, without the consent of Moses; and their defeat.

entries.label: II
entries.original: THE SEDITION OF CORAH AND OF THE MULTITUDE AGAINST MOSES, AND AGAINST HIS BROTHER, CONCERNING THE PRIESTHOOD.
entries.display: The sedition of Corah and of the multitude against Moses, and against his brother, concerning the priesthood.

entries.label: III
entries.original: HOW THOSE THAT STIRRED UP THIS SEDITION WERE DESTROYED, ACCORDING TO THE WILL OF GOD; AND HOW AARON, MOSES'S BROTHER, BOTH HE AND HIS POSTERITY, RETAINED THE PRIESTHOOD.
entries.display: How those that stirred up this sedition were destroyed, according to the will of God; and how Aaron, Moses's brother, both he and his posterity, retained the priesthood.

entries.label: IV
entries.original: WHAT HAPPENED TO THE HEBREWS DURING THIRTY-EIGHT YEARS IN THE WILDERNESS.
entries.display: What happened to the Hebrews during thirty-eight years in the wilderness.

entries.label: V
entries.original: HOW MOSES CONQUERED SIHON AND OG, KINGS OF THE AMORITES, AND DESTROYED THEIR WHOLE ARMY, AND THEN DIVIDED THEIR LAND BY LOT TO TWO TRIBES AND A HALF OF THE HEBREWS.
entries.display: How Moses conquered Sihon and Og, kings of the Amorites, and destroyed their whole army, and then divided their land by lot to two tribes and a half of the Hebrews.

entries.label: VI
entries.original: CONCERNING BALAAM THE PROPHET, AND WHAT KIND OF MAN HE WAS.
entries.display: Concerning Balaam the prophet, and what kind of man he was.

entries.label: VII
entries.original: HOW THE HEBREWS FOUGHT WITH THE MIDIANITES, AND OVERCAME THEM.
entries.display: How the Hebrews fought with the Midianites, and overcame them.

entries.label: VIII
entries.original: THE POLITY SETTLED BY MOSES; AND HOW HE DISAPPEARED FROM AMONG MANKIND.
entries.display: The polity settled by Moses; and how he disappeared from among mankind.

entries.label: I
entries.original: HOW JOSHUA, THE COMMANDER OF THE HEBREWS, MADE WAR WITH THE CANAANITES, AND OVERCAME THEM, AND DESTROYED THEM, AND DIVIDED THEIR LAND BY LOT TO THE TRIBES OF ISRAEL.
entries.display: How Joshua, the commander of the Hebrews, made war with the Canaanites, and overcame them, and destroyed them, and divided their land by lot to the tribes of Israel.

entries.label: II
entries.original: HOW, AFTER THE DEATH OF JOSHUA THEIR COMMANDER, THE ISRAELITES TRANSGRESSED THE LAWS OF THEIR COUNTRY, AND EXPERIENCED GREAT AFFLICTIONS; AND WHEN THERE WAS A SEDITION ARISEN, THE TRIBE OF BENJAMIN WAS DESTROYED, EXCEPTING ONLY SIX HUNDRED MEN.
entries.display: How, after the death of Joshua their commander, the Israelites transgressed the laws of their country, and experienced great afflictions; and when there was a sedition arisen, the tribe of Benjamin was destroyed, excepting only six hundred men.

entries.label: III
entries.original: HOW THE ISRAELITES AFTER THIS MISFORTUNE GREW WICKED, AND SERVED THE ASSYRIANS; AND HOW GOD DELIVERED THEM BY OTHNIEL, WHO RULED OVER THEM FORTY YEARS.
entries.display: How the Israelites after this misfortune grew wicked, and served the Assyrians; and how God delivered them by Othniel, who ruled over them forty years.

entries.label: IV
entries.original: HOW OUR PEOPLE SERVED THE MOABITES EIGHTEEN YEARS, AND WERE THEN DELIVERED FROM SLAVERY BY ONE EHUD, WHO RETAINED THE DOMINION EIGHTY YEARS.
entries.display: How our people served the Moabites eighteen years, and were then delivered from slavery by one Ehud, who retained the dominion eighty years.

entries.label: V
entries.original: HOW THE CANAANITES BROUGHT THE ISRAELITES UNDER SLAVERY FOR TWENTY YEARS; AFTER WHICH THEY WERE DELIVERED BY BARAK AND DEBORAH, WHO RULED OVER THEM FOR FORTY YEARS.
entries.display: How the Canaanites brought the Israelites under slavery for twenty years; after which they were delivered by Barak and Deborah, who ruled over them for forty years.

entries.label: VI
entries.original: HOW THE MIDIANITES AND OTHER NATIONS FOUGHT AGAINST THE ISRAELITES, AND BEAT THEM, AND AFFLICTED THEIR COUNTRY FOR SEVEN YEARS. HOW THEY WERE DELIVERED BY GIDEON, WHO RULED OVER THE MULTITUDE FOR FORTY YEARS.
entries.display: How the Midianites and other nations fought against the Israelites, and beat them, and afflicted their country for seven years. How they were delivered by Gideon, who ruled over the multitude for forty years.

entries.label: VII
entries.original: THAT THE JUDGES WHO SUCCEEDED GIDEON MADE WAR WITH THE ADJOINING NATIONS FOR A LONG TIME.
entries.display: That the judges who succeeded Gideon made war with the adjoining nations for a long time.

entries.label: VIII
entries.original: CONCERNING THE FORTITUDE OF SAMSON, AND WHAT MISCHIEFS HE BROUGHT UPON THE PHILISTINES.
entries.display: Concerning the fortitude of Samson, and what mischiefs he brought upon the Philistines.

entries.label: IX
entries.original: HOW UNDER ELI'S GOVERNMENT OF THE ISRAELITES, BOOZ MARRIED RUTH, FROM WHOM CAME OBED, THE GRANDFATHER OF DAVID.
entries.display: How under Eli's government of the Israelites, Booz married Ruth, from whom came Obed, the grandfather of David.

entries.label: X
entries.original: CONCERNING THE BIRTH OF SAMUEL; AND HOW HE FORETOLD THE CALAMITY THAT BEFELL THE SONS OF ELI.
entries.display: Concerning the birth of Samuel; and how he foretold the calamity that befell the sons of Eli.

entries.label: XI
entries.original: HEREIN IS DECLARED WHAT BEFELL THE SONS OF ELI, THE ARK, AND THE PEOPLE; AND HOW ELI HIMSELF DIED MISERABLY.
entries.display: Herein is declared what befell the sons of Eli, the ark, and the people; and how Eli himself died miserably.

entries.label: I
entries.original: THE DESTRUCTION THAT CAME UPON THE PHILISTINES, AND UPON THEIR LAND, BY THE WRATH OF GOD, ON ACCOUNT OF THEIR HAVING CARRIED THE ARK AWAY CAPTIVE; AND AFTER WHAT MANNER THEY SENT IT BACK TO THE HEBREWS.
entries.display: The destruction that came upon the Philistines, and upon their land, by the wrath of God, on account of their having carried the ark away captive; and after what manner they sent it back to the Hebrews.

entries.label: II
entries.original: THE EXPEDITION OF THE PHILISTINES AGAINST THE HEBREWS, AND THE HEBREWS' VICTORY UNDER THE CONDUCT OF SAMUEL THE PROPHET, WHO WAS THEIR GENERAL.
entries.display: The expedition of the Philistines against the Hebrews, and the Hebrews' victory under the conduct of Samuel the prophet, who was their general.

entries.label: III
entries.original: HOW SAMUEL, WHEN HE WAS SO INFIRM WITH OLD AGE THAT HE COULD NOT TAKE CARE OF THE PUBLIC AFFAIRS, INTRUSTED THEM TO HIS SONS; AND HOW, UPON THE EVIL ADMINISTRATION OF THE GOVERNMENT BY THEM, THE MULTITUDE WERE SO ANGRY, THAT THEY REQUIRED TO HAVE A KING TO GOVERN THEM, ALTHOUGH SAMUEL WAS MUCH DISPLEASED THEREAT.
entries.display: How Samuel, when he was so infirm with old age that he could not take care of the public affairs, intrusted them to his sons; and how, upon the evil administration of the government by them, the multitude were so angry, that they required to have a king to govern them, although Samuel was much displeased thereat.

entries.label: IV
entries.original: THE APPOINTMENT OF A KING OVER THE ISRAELITES, WHOSE NAME WAS SAUL; AND THIS BY THE COMMAND OF GOD.
entries.display: The appointment of a king over the Israelites, whose name was Saul; and this by the command of God.

entries.label: V
entries.original: SAUL'S EXPEDITION AGAINST THE NATION OF THE AMORITES, AND VICTORY OVER THEM, AND THE SPOILS HE TOOK FROM THEM.
entries.display: Saul's expedition against the nation of the Amorites, and victory over them, and the spoils he took from them.

entries.label: VI
entries.original: HOW THE PHILISTINES MADE ANOTHER EXPEDITION AGAINST THE HEBREWS, AND WERE BEATEN.
entries.display: How the Philistines made another expedition against the Hebrews, and were beaten.

entries.label: VII
entries.original: SAUL'S WAR WITH THE AMALEKITES, AND CONQUEST OF THEM.
entries.display: Saul's war with the Amalekites, and conquest of them.

entries.label: VIII
entries.original: HOW, UPON SAUL'S TRANSGRESSION OF THE PROPHET'S COMMANDS, SAMUEL ORDAINED ANOTHER PERSON TO BE KING PRIVATELY, WHOSE NAME WAS DAVID, AS GOD COMMANDED HIM.
entries.display: How, upon Saul's transgression of the prophet's commands, Samuel ordained another person to be king privately, whose name was David, as God commanded him.

entries.label: IX
entries.original: HOW THE PHILISTINES MADE ANOTHER EXPEDITION AGAINST THE HEBREWS, UNDER THE REIGN OF SAUL; AND HOW THEY WERE OVERCOME BY DAVID'S SLAYING GOLIATH IN SINGLE COMBAT.
entries.display: How the Philistines made another expedition against the Hebrews, under the reign of Saul; and how they were overcome by David's slaying Goliath in single combat.

entries.label: X
entries.original: SAUL ENVIES DAVID FOR HIS GLORIOUS SUCCESS, AND TAKES AN OCCASION OF ENTRAPPING HIM, FROM THE PROMISE HE MADE HIM OF GIVING HIM HIS DAUGHTER IN MARRIAGE; BUT THIS UPON CONDITION OF HIS BRINGING HIM SIX HUNDRED HEADS OF THE PHILISTINES.
entries.display: Saul envies David for his glorious success, and takes an occasion of entrapping him, from the promise he made him of giving him his daughter in marriage; but this upon condition of his bringing him six hundred heads of the Philistines.

entries.label: XI
entries.original: HOW DAVID, UPON SAUL'S LAYING SNARES FOR HIM, DID YET ESCAPE THE DANGERS HE WAS IN, BY THE AFFECTION AND CARE OF JONATHAN, AND THE CONTRIVANCES OF HIS WIFE MICHAL; AND HOW HE CAME TO SAMUEL THE PROPHET.
entries.display: How David, upon Saul's laying snares for him, did yet escape the dangers he was in, by the affection and care of Jonathan, and the contrivances of his wife Michal; and how he came to Samuel the prophet.

entries.label: XII
entries.original: HOW DAVID FLED TO AHIMELECH, AND AFTERWARDS TO THE KINGS OF THE PHILISTINES, AND OF THE MOABITES; AND HOW SAUL SLEW AHIMELECH AND HIS FAMILY.
entries.display: How David fled to Ahimelech, and afterwards to the kings of the Philistines, and of the Moabites; and how Saul slew Ahimelech and his family.

entries.label: XIII
entries.original: HOW DAVID, WHEN HE HAD TWICE THE OPPORTUNITY OF KILLING SAUL, DID NOT KILL HIM. ALSO, CONCERNING THE DEATH OF SAMUEL AND NABAL.
entries.display: How David, when he had twice the opportunity of killing Saul, did not kill him. Also, concerning the death of Samuel and Nabal.

entries.label: XIV
entries.original: HOW SAUL, UPON GOD'S NOT ANSWERING HIM CONCERNING THE FIGHT WITH THE PHILISTINES, DESIRED A NECROMANTIC WOMAN TO RAISE UP THE SOUL OF SAMUEL TO HIM; AND HOW HE DIED, WITH HIS SONS, UPON THE OVERTHROW OF THE HEBREWS IN BATTLE.
entries.display: How Saul, upon God's not answering him concerning the fight with the Philistines, desired a necromantic woman to raise up the soul of Samuel to him; and how he died, with his sons, upon the overthrow of the Hebrews in battle.

entries.label: I
entries.original: HOW DAVID REIGNED OVER ONE TRIBE AT HEBRON, WHILE THE SON OF SAUL REIGNED OVER THE REST OF THE MULTITUDE; AND HOW, IN THE CIVIL WAR WHICH THEN AROSE, ASAHEL AND ABNER WERE SLAIN.
entries.display: How David reigned over one tribe at Hebron, while the son of Saul reigned over the rest of the multitude; and how, in the civil war which then arose, Asahel and Abner were slain.

entries.label: II
entries.original: THAT UPON THE SLAUGHTER OF ISHBOSHETH, BY THE TREACHERY OF HIS FRIENDS, DAVID RECEIVED THE WHOLE KINGDOM.
entries.display: That upon the slaughter of Ishbosheth, by the treachery of his friends, David received the whole kingdom.

entries.label: III
entries.original: HOW DAVID LAID SEIGE TO JERUSALEM; AND WHEN HE HAD TAKEN THE CITY, HE CAST THE CANAANITES OUT OF IT, AND BROUGHT IN THE JEWS TO INHABIT THEREIN.
entries.display: How David laid seige to Jerusalem; and when he had taken the city, he cast the Canaanites out of it, and brought in the Jews to inhabit therein.

entries.label: IV
entries.original: THAT WHEN DAVID HAD CONQUERED THE PHILISTINES, WHO MADE WAR AGAINST HIM AT JERUSALEM, HE REMOVED THE ARK TO JERUSALEM, AND HAD A MIND TO BUILD A TEMPLE.
entries.display: That when David had conquered the Philistines, who made war against him at Jerusalem, he removed the ark to Jerusalem, and had a mind to build a temple.

entries.label: V
entries.original: HOW DAVID BROUGHT UNDER THE PHILISTINES, AND THE MOABITES, AND THE KINGS OF SOPHENE, AND OF DAMASCUS, AND OF THE SYRIANS, AS ALSO THE IDUMEANS, IN WAR; AND HOW HE MADE A LEAGUE WITH THE KING OF HAMATH; AND WAS MINDFUL OF THE FRIENDSHIP THAT JONATHAN, THE SON OF SAUL, HAD BORNE TO HIM.
entries.display: How David brought under the Philistines, and the Moabites, and the kings of Sophene, and of Damascus, and of the Syrians, as also the Idumeans, in war; and how he made a league with the king of Hamath; and was mindful of the friendship that Jonathan, the son of Saul, had borne to him.

entries.label: VI
entries.original: HOW THE WAR WAS WAGED AGAINST THE AMMONITES, AND HAPPILY CONCLUDED.
entries.display: How the war was waged against the Ammonites, and happily concluded.

entries.label: VII
entries.original: HOW DAVID FELL IN LOVE WITH BATHSHEBA, AND SLEW HER HUSBAND URIAH, FOR WHICH HE IS REPROVED BY NATHAN.
entries.display: How David fell in love with Bathsheba, and slew her husband Uriah, for which he is reproved by Nathan.

entries.label: VIII
entries.original: HOW ABSALOM MURDERED AMNON, WHO HAD FORCED HIS OWN SISTER; AND HOW HE WAS BANISHED, AND AFTERWARDS RECALLED BY DAVID.
entries.display: How Absalom murdered Amnon, who had forced his own sister; and how he was banished, and afterwards recalled by David.

entries.label: IX
entries.original: CONCERNING THE INSURRECTION OF ABSALOM AGAINST DAVID; AND CONCERNING AHITHOPHEL AND HUSHAI; AND CONCERNING ZIBA AND SHIMEI; AND HOW AHITHOPHEL HANGED HIMSELF.
entries.display: Concerning the insurrection of Absalom against David; and concerning Ahithophel and Hushai; and concerning Ziba and Shimei; and how Ahithophel hanged himself.

entries.label: X
entries.original: HOW, WHEN ABSALOM WAS BEATEN, HE WAS CAUGHT IN A TREE BY HIS HAIR, AND WAS SLAIN.
entries.display: How, when Absalom was beaten, he was caught in a tree by his hair, and was slain.

entries.label: XI
entries.original: HOW DAVID, WHEN HE HAD RECOVERED HIS KINGDOM, WAS RECONCILED TO SHIMEI, AND TO ZIBA; AND SHOWED A GREAT AFFECTION TO BARZILLAI: AND HOW, UPON THE RISE OF A SEDITION, HE MADE AMASA CAPTAIN OF HIS HOST, IN ORDER TO PURSUE SHEBA; WHICH AMASA WAS SLAIN BY JOAB.
entries.display: How David, when he had recovered his kingdom, was reconciled to Shimei, and to Ziba; and showed a great affection to Barzillai: and how, upon the rise of a sedition, he made Amasa captain of his host, in order to pursue Sheba; which Amasa was slain by Joab.

entries.label: XII
entries.original: HOW THE HEBREWS WERE DELIVERED FROM A FAMINE WHEN THE GIBEONITES HAD CAUSED PUNISHMENT TO BE INFLICTED FOR THOSE OF THEM THAT HAD BEEN SLAIN: AS ALSO, WHAT GREAT ACTIONS WERE PERFORMED AGAINST THE PHILISTINES BY DAVID, AND THE MEN OF VALOUR ABOUT HIM.
entries.display: How the Hebrews were delivered from a famine when the Gibeonites had caused punishment to be inflicted for those of them that had been slain: as also, what great actions were performed against the Philistines by David, and the men of valour about him.

entries.label: XIII
entries.original: THAT WHEN DAVID HAD NUMBERED THE PEOPLE, THEY WERE PUNISHED; AND HOW THE DIVINE COMPASSION RESTRAINED THAT PUNISHMENT.
entries.display: That when David had numbered the people, they were punished; and how the divine compassion restrained that punishment.

entries.label: XIV
entries.original: THAT DAVID MADE GREAT PREPARATIONS FOR THE HOUSE OF GOD; AND THAT UPON ADONIJAH'S ATTEMPT TO GAIN THE KINGDOM, HE APPOINTED SOLOMON TO REIGN.
entries.display: That David made great preparations for the house of God; and that upon Adonijah's attempt to gain the kingdom, he appointed Solomon to reign.

entries.label: XV
entries.original: WHAT CHARGE DAVID GAVE TO HIS SON SOLOMON AT THE APPROACH OF HIS DEATH; AND HOW MANY THINGS HE LEFT HIM FOR THE BUILDING OF THE TEMPLE.
entries.display: What charge David gave to his son Solomon at the approach of his death; and how many things he left him for the building of the temple.

entries.label: I
entries.original: HOW SOLOMON, WHEN HE HAD RECEIVED THE KINGDOM, TOOK OFF HIS ENEMIES.
entries.display: How Solomon, when he had received the kingdom, took off his enemies.

entries.label: II
entries.original: CONCERNING THE WIFE OF SOLOMON; CONCERNING HIS WISDOM AND RICHES; AND CONCERNING WHAT HE OBTAINED OF HIRAM FOR THE BUILDING OF THE TEMPLE.
entries.display: Concerning the wife of Solomon; concerning his wisdom and riches; and concerning what he obtained of Hiram for the building of the temple.

entries.label: III
entries.original: OF THE BUILDING OF THE TEMPLE.
entries.display: Of the building of the temple.

entries.label: IV
entries.original: HOW SOLOMON REMOVED THE ARK INTO THE TEMPLE; HOW HE MADE SUPPLICATION TO GOD, AND OFFERED PUBLIC SACRIFICES TO HIM.
entries.display: How Solomon removed the ark into the temple; how he made supplication to God, and offered public sacrifices to him.

entries.label: V
entries.original: HOW SOLOMON BUILT HIMSELF A ROYAL PALACE, VERY COSTLY AND SPLENDID; AND HOW HE SOLVED THE RIDDLES WHICH WERE SENT HIM BY HIRAM.
entries.display: How Solomon built himself a royal palace, very costly and splendid; and how he solved the riddles which were sent him by Hiram.

entries.label: VI
entries.original: HOW SOLOMON FORTIFIED THE CITY OF JERUSALEM, AND BUILT GREAT CITIES; AND HOW HE BROUGHT SOME OF THE CANAANITES INTO SUBJECTION, AND ENTERTAINED THE QUEEN OF EGYPT AND OF ETHIOPIA.
entries.display: How Solomon fortified the city of Jerusalem, and built great cities; and how he brought some of the Canaanites into subjection, and entertained the queen of Egypt and of Ethiopia.

entries.label: VII
entries.original: HOW SOLOMON GREW RICH, AND FELL DESPERATELY IN LOVE WITH WOMEN, AND HOW GOD, BEING INCENSED AT IT, RAISED UP ADER AND JEROBOAM AGAINST HIM. CONCERNING THE DEATH OF SOLOMON.
entries.display: How Solomon grew rich, and fell desperately in love with women, and how God, being incensed at it, raised up Ader and Jeroboam against him. Concerning the death of Solomon.

entries.label: VIII
entries.original: HOW, UPON THE DEATH OF SOLOMON, THE PEOPLE FORSOOK HIS SON REHOBOAM, AND ORDAINED JEROBOAM KING OVER THE TEN TRIBES.
entries.display: How, upon the death of Solomon, the people forsook his son Rehoboam, and ordained Jeroboam king over the ten tribes.

entries.label: IX
entries.original: HOW JADON THE PROPHET WAS PERSUADED BY ANOTHER LYING PROPHET, AND RETURNED [TO BETHEL], AND WAS AFTERWARDS SLAIN BY A LION. AS ALSO WHAT WORDS THE WICKED PROPHET MADE USE OF TO PERSUADE THE KING, AND THEREBY ALIENATED HIS MIND FROM GOD.
entries.display: How Jadon the prophet was persuaded by another lying prophet, and returned [to Bethel], and was afterwards slain by a lion. As also what words the wicked prophet made use of to persuade the king, and thereby alienated his mind from God.

entries.label: X
entries.original: CONCERNING REHOBOAM, AND HOW GOD INFLICTED PUNISHMENT UPON HIM FOR HIS IMPIETY, BY SHISHAK [KING OF EGYPT].
entries.display: Concerning Rehoboam, and how God inflicted punishment upon him for his impiety, by Shishak [king of Egypt].

entries.label: XI
entries.original: CONCERNING THE DEATH OF A SON OF JEROBOAM. HOW JEROBOAM WAS BEATEN BY ABIJAH, WHO DIED A LITTLE AFTERWARDS, AND WAS SUCCEEDED IN HIS KINGDOM BY ASA. AND ALSO HOW, AFTER THE DEATH OF JEROBOAM, BAASHA DESTROYED HIS SON NADAB, AND ALL THE HOUSE OF JEROBOAM.
entries.display: Concerning the death of a son of Jeroboam. How Jeroboam was beaten by Abijah, who died a little afterwards, and was succeeded in his kingdom by Asa. And also how, after the death of Jeroboam, Baasha destroyed his son Nadab, and all the house of Jeroboam.

entries.label: XII
entries.original: HOW ZERAH, KING OF THE ETHIOPIANS, WAS BEATEN BY ASA; AND HOW ASA, UPON BAASHA'S MAKING WAR AGAINST HIM, INVITED THE KING OF THE DAMASCENS TO ASSIST HIM; AND HOW, ON THE DESTRUCTION OF THE HOUSE OF BAASHA, ZIMRI GOT THE KINGDOM, AS DID HIS SON AHAB AFTER HIM.
entries.display: How Zerah, king of the Ethiopians, was beaten by Asa; and how Asa, upon Baasha's making war against him, invited the king of the Damascens to assist him; and how, on the destruction of the house of Baasha, Zimri got the kingdom, as did his son Ahab after him.

entries.label: XIII
entries.original: HOW AHAB, WHEN HE HAD TAKEN JEZEBEL TO WIFE, BECAME MORE WICKED THAN ALL THE KINGS THAT HAD BEEN BEFORE HIM. OF THE ACTIONS OF THE PROPHET ELIJAH; AND WHAT BEFEL NABOTH.
entries.display: How Ahab, when he had taken Jezebel to wife, became more wicked than all the kings that had been before him. Of the actions of the prophet Elijah; and what befel Naboth.

entries.label: XIV
entries.original: HOW HADAD, KING OF DAMASCUS AND OF SYRIA, MADE TWO EXPEDITIONS AGAINST AHAB, AND WAS BEATEN.
entries.display: How Hadad, king of Damascus and of Syria, made two expeditions against Ahab, and was beaten.

entries.label: XV
entries.original: CONCERNING JEHOSHAPHAT, THE KING OF JERUSALEM; AND HOW AHAB MADE AN EXPEDITION AGAINST THE SYRIANS, AND WAS ASSISTED THEREIN BY JEHOSHAPHAT, BUT WAS HIMSELF OVERCOME IN BATTLE, AND PERISHED THEREIN.
entries.display: Concerning Jehoshaphat, the king of Jerusalem; and how Ahab made an expedition against the Syrians, and was assisted therein by Jehoshaphat, but was himself overcome in battle, and perished therein.

entries.label: I
entries.original: CONCERNING JEHOSHAPHAT AGAIN; HOW HE CONSTITUTED JUDGES, AND, BY GOD'S ASSISTANCE, OVERCAME HIS ENEMIES.
entries.display: Concerning Jehoshaphat again; how he constituted judges, and, by God's assistance, overcame his enemies.

entries.label: II
entries.original: CONCERNING AHAZIAH, THE KING OF ISRAEL; AND AGAIN CONCERNING THE PROPHET ELIJAH.
entries.display: Concerning Ahaziah, the king of Israel; and again concerning the prophet Elijah.

entries.label: III
entries.original: HOW JORAM AND JEHOSHAPHAT MADE AN EXPEDITION AGAINST THE MOABITES; AS ALSO CONCERNING THE WONDERS OF ELISHA, AND THE DEATH OF JEHOSHAPHAT.
entries.display: How Joram and Jehoshaphat made an expedition against the Moabites; as also concerning the wonders of Elisha, and the death of Jehoshaphat.

entries.label: IV
entries.original: JEHORAM SUCCEEDS JEHOSHAPHAT; HOW JORAM, HIS NAMESAKE, KING OF ISRAEL, FOUGHT WITH THE SYRIANS; AND WHAT WONDERS WERE DONE BY THE PROPHET ELISHA.
entries.display: Jehoram succeeds Jehoshaphat; how Joram, his namesake, king of Israel, fought with the Syrians; and what wonders were done by the prophet Elisha.

entries.label: V
entries.original: CONCERNING THE WICKEDNESS OF JEHORAM, KING OF JERUSALEM; HIS DEFEAT, AND DEATH.
entries.display: Concerning the wickedness of Jehoram, king of Jerusalem; his defeat, and death.

entries.label: VI
entries.original: HOW JEHU WAS ANOINTED KING, AND SLEW BOTH JORAM AND AHAZIAH; AS ALSO WHAT HE DID FOR THE PUNISHMENT OF THE WICKED.
entries.display: How Jehu was anointed king, and slew both Joram and Ahaziah; as also what he did for the punishment of the wicked.

entries.label: VII
entries.original: HOW ATHALIAH REIGNED OVER JERUSALEM FOR FIVE [SIX] YEARS, WHEN JEHOIADA THE HIGH-PRIEST SLEW HER, AND MADE JEHOASH, THE SON OF AHAZIAH, KING.
entries.display: How Athaliah reigned over Jerusalem for five [six] years, when Jehoiada the high-priest slew her, and made Jehoash, the son of Ahaziah, king.

entries.label: VIII
entries.original: HAZAEL MAKES AN EXPEDITION AGAINST THE PEOPLE OF ISRAEL AND THE INHABITANTS OF JERUSALEM. JEHU DIES, AND JEHOAHAZ SUCCEEDS IN THE GOVERNMENT. JEHOASH, THE KING OF JERUSALEM, AT FIRST IS CAREFUL ABOUT THE WORSHIP OF GOD, BUT AFTERWARDS BECOMES IMPIOUS, AND COMMANDS ZECHARIAH TO BE STONED. WHEN JEHOASH [KING OF JUDAH] WAS DEAD, AMAZIAH SUCCEEDS HIM IN THE KINGDOM.
entries.display: Hazael makes an expedition against the people of Israel and the inhabitants of Jerusalem. Jehu dies, and Jehoahaz succeeds in the government. Jehoash, the king of Jerusalem, at first is careful about the worship of God, but afterwards becomes impious, and commands Zechariah to be stoned. When Jehoash [king of Judah] was dead, Amaziah succeeds him in the kingdom.

entries.label: IX
entries.original: HOW AMAZIAH MADE AN EXPEDITION AGAINST THE EDOMITES AND AMALEKITES, AND CONQUERED THEM; BUT WHEN HE AFTERWARDS MADE WAR AGAINST JOASH, HE WAS BEATEN, AND NOT LONG AFTER WAS SLAIN; AND UZZIAH SUCCEEDED IN THE GOVERNMENT.
entries.display: How Amaziah made an expedition against the Edomites and Amalekites, and conquered them; but when he afterwards made war against Joash, he was beaten, and not long after was slain; and Uzziah succeeded in the government.

entries.label: X
entries.original: CONCERNING JEROBOAM, KING OF ISRAEL, AND JONAH, THE PROPHET; AND HOW, AFTER THE DEATH OF JEROBOAM, HIS SON ZECHARIAH TOOK THE GOVERNMENT. HOW UZZIAH, KING OF JERUSALEM, SUBDUED THE NATIONS THAT WERE ROUND ABOUT HIM, AND WHAT BEFELL HIM WHEN HE ATTEMPTED TO OFFER INCENSE TO GOD.
entries.display: Concerning Jeroboam, king of Israel, and Jonah, the prophet; and how, after the death of Jeroboam, his son Zechariah took the government. How Uzziah, king of Jerusalem, subdued the nations that were round about him, and what befell him when he attempted to offer incense to God.

entries.label: XI
entries.original: HOW ZECHARIAH, SHALLUM, MENAHEM, PEKAHIAH, AND PEKAH, TOOK THE GOVERNMENT OVER THE ISRAELITES; AND HOW PUL AND TIGLATH-PILESER MADE AN EXPEDITION AGAINST THE ISRAELITES. HOW JOTHAM, THE SON OF UZZIAH, REIGNED OVER THE TRIBE OF JUDAH; AND WHAT THINGS NAHUM PROPHESIED AGAINST THE ASSYRIANS.
entries.display: How Zechariah, Shallum, Menahem, Pekahiah, and Pekah, took the government over the Israelites; and how Pul and Tiglath-Pileser made an expedition against the Israelites. How Jotham, the son of Uzziah, reigned over the tribe of Judah; and what things Nahum prophesied against the Assyrians.

entries.label: XII
entries.original: HOW, UPON THE DEATH OF JOTHAM, AHAZ REIGNED IN HIS STEAD; AGAINST WHOM REZIN, KING OF SYRIA, AND PEKAH, KING OF ISRAEL, MADE WAR; AND HOW TIGLATH-PILESER, KING OF ASSYRIA, CAME TO THE ASSISTANCE OF AHAZ, AND LAID SYRIA WASTE, AND REMOVING THE DAMASCENS INTO MEDIA, PLACED OTHER NATIONS IN THEIR ROOM.
entries.display: How, upon the death of Jotham, Ahaz reigned in his stead; against whom Rezin, king of Syria, and Pekah, king of Israel, made war; and how Tiglath-Pileser, king of Assyria, came to the assistance of Ahaz, and laid Syria waste, and removing the Damascens into Media, placed other nations in their room.

entries.label: XIII
entries.original: HOW PEKAH DIED BY THE TREACHERY OF HOSHEA, WHO WAS A LITTLE AFTER SUBDUED BY SHALMANESER; AND HOW HEZEKIAH REIGNED INSTEAD OF AHAZ; AND WHAT ACTIONS OF PIETY AND JUSTICE HE DID.
entries.display: How Pekah died by the treachery of Hoshea, who was a little after subdued by Shalmaneser; and how Hezekiah reigned instead of Ahaz; and what actions of piety and justice he did.

entries.label: XIV
entries.original: HOW SHALMANESER TOOK SAMARIA BY FORCE, AND HOW HE TRANSPLANTED THE TEN TRIBES INTO MEDIA, AND BROUGHT THE NATION OF THE CUTHEANS INTO THEIR COUNTRY [IN THEIR ROOM].
entries.display: How Shalmaneser took Samaria by force, and how he transplanted the ten tribes into Media, and brought the nation of the Cutheans into their country [in their room].

entries.label: I
entries.original: HOW SENNACHERIB MADE AN EXPEDITION AGAINST HEZEKIAH; WHAT THREATENINGS RABSHAKEH MADE TO HEZEKIAH WHEN SENNACHERIB WAS GONE AGAINST THE EGYPTIANS; HOW ISAIAH THE PROPHET ENCOURAGED HIM; HOW SENNACHERIB, HAVING FAILED OF SUCCESS IN EGYPT, RETURNED THENCE TO JERUSALEM; AND HOW, UPON HIS FINDING HIS ARMY DESTROYED, HE RETURNED HOME; AND WHAT BEFELL HIM A LITTLE AFTERWARD.
entries.display: How Sennacherib made an expedition against Hezekiah; what threatenings Rabshakeh made to Hezekiah when Sennacherib was gone against the Egyptians; how Isaiah the prophet encouraged him; how Sennacherib, having failed of success in Egypt, returned thence to Jerusalem; and how, upon his finding his army destroyed, he returned home; and what befell him a little afterward.

entries.label: II
entries.original: HOW HEZEKIAH WAS SICK, AND READY TO DIE, AND HOW GOD BESTOWED UPON HIM FIFTEEN YEARS LONGER LIFE [AND SECURED THAT PROMISE], BY THE GOING BACK OF THE SHADOW TEN DEGREES.
entries.display: How Hezekiah was sick, and ready to die, and how God bestowed upon him fifteen years longer life [and secured that promise], by the going back of the shadow ten degrees.

entries.label: III
entries.original: HOW MANASSEH REIGNED AFTER HEZEKIAH; AND HOW, WHEN HE WAS IN CAPTIVITY, HE RETURNED TO GOD, AND WAS RESTORED TO HIS KINGDOM, AND LEFT IT TO [HIS SON] AMON.
entries.display: How Manasseh reigned after Hezekiah; and how, when he was in captivity, he returned to God, and was restored to his kingdom, and left it to [his son] Amon.

entries.label: IV
entries.original: HOW AMON REIGNED INSTEAD OF MANASSEH; AND AFTER AMON, REIGNED JOSIAH; HE WAS BOTH RIGHTEOUS AND RELIGIOUS. AS ALSO CONCERNING HULDAH THE PROPHETESS.
entries.display: How Amon reigned instead of Manasseh; and after Amon, reigned Josiah; he was both righteous and religious. As also concerning Huldah the prophetess.

entries.label: V
entries.original: HOW JOSIAH FOUGHT WITH NECO [KING OF EGYPT], AND WAS WOUNDED AND DIED IN A LITTLE TIME. AFTERWARDS: AS ALSO HOW NECO CARRIED JEHOAHAZ, WHO HAD BEEN MADE KING, INTO EGYPT, AND DELIVERED THE KINGDOM TO JEHOIAKIM: AND [LASTLY], CONCERNING JEREMIAH AND EZEKIEL.
entries.display: How Josiah fought with Neco [king of Egypt], and was wounded and died in a little time. Afterwards: as also how Neco carried Jehoahaz, who had been made king, into Egypt, and delivered the kingdom to Jehoiakim: and [lastly], concerning Jeremiah and Ezekiel.

entries.label: VI
entries.original: HOW NEBUCHADNEZZAR, WHEN HE HAD CONQUERED THE KING OF EGYPT, MADE AN EXPEDITION AGAINST THE JEWS, AND SLEW JEHOIAKIM, AND MADE JEHOIACHIN, HIS SON, KING.
entries.display: How Nebuchadnezzar, when he had conquered the king of Egypt, made an expedition against the Jews, and slew Jehoiakim, and made Jehoiachin, his son, king.

entries.label: VII
entries.original: THAT THE KING OF BABYLON REPENTED OF MAKING JEHOIACHIN KING, AND TOOK HIM AWAY TO BABYLON, AND DELIVERED THE KINGDOM TO ZEDEKIAH. THIS KING WOULD NOT BELIEVE WHAT WAS PREDICTED BY JEREMIAH AND EZEKIEL, BUT JOINED HIMSELF TO THE EGYPTIANS; WHO, WHEN THEY CAME INTO JUDEA, WERE VANQUISHED BY THE KING OF BABYLON; AS ALSO WHAT BEFELL JEREMIAH.
entries.display: That the king of Babylon repented of making Jehoiachin king, and took him away to Babylon, and delivered the kingdom to Zedekiah. This king would not believe what was predicted by Jeremiah and Ezekiel, but joined himself to the Egyptians; who, when they came into Judea, were vanquished by the king of Babylon; as also what befell Jeremiah.

entries.label: VIII
entries.original: HOW THE KING OF BABYLON TOOK JERUSALEM AND BURNT THE TEMPLE, AND REMOVED THE PEOPLE OF JERUSALEM AND ZEDEKIAH TO BABYLON. AS ALSO, WHO THEY WERE THAT HAD SUCCEEDED IN THE HIGH-PRIESTHOOD UNDER THE KINGS.
entries.display: How the king of Babylon took Jerusalem and burnt the temple, and removed the people of Jerusalem and Zedekiah to Babylon. As also, who they were that had succeeded in the high-priesthood under the kings.

entries.label: IX
entries.original: HOW NEBUZARADAN SET GEDALIAH OVER THE JEWS THAT WERE LEFT IN JUDEA, WHICH GEDALIAH WAS, A LITTLE AFTERWARD, SLAIN BY ISHMAEL; AND HOW JOHANAN, AFTER ISHMAEL WAS DRIVEN AWAY, WENT DOWN INTO EGYPT WITH THE PEOPLE; WHICH PEOPLE NEBUCHADNEZZAR, WHEN HE MADE AN EXPEDITION AGAINST THE EGYPTIANS, TOOK CAPTIVE, AND BROUGHT THEM AWAY TO BABYLON.
entries.display: How Nebuzaradan set Gedaliah over the Jews that were left in Judea, which Gedaliah was, a little afterward, slain by Ishmael; and how Johanan, after Ishmael was driven away, went down into Egypt with the people; which people Nebuchadnezzar, when he made an expedition against the Egyptians, took captive, and brought them away to Babylon.

entries.label: X
entries.original: CONCERNING DANIEL, AND WHAT BEFEL HIM AT BABYLON.
entries.display: Concerning Daniel, and what befel him at Babylon.

entries.label: XI
entries.original: CONCERNING NEBUCHADNEZZAR AND HIS SUCCESSORS, AND HOW THEIR GOVERNMENT WAS DISSOLVED BY THE PERSIANS; AND WHAT THINGS BEFELL DANIEL IN MEDIA; AND WHAT PROPHECIES HE DELIVERED THERE.
entries.display: Concerning Nebuchadnezzar and his successors, and how their government was dissolved by the Persians; and what things befell Daniel in Media; and what prophecies he delivered there.

entries.label: I
entries.original: HOW CYRUS, KING OF THE PERSIANS, DELIVERED THE JEWS OUT OF BABYLON, AND SUFFERED THEM TO RETURN TO THEIR OWN COUNTRY, AND TO BUILD THEIR TEMPLE; FOR WHICH WORK HE GAVE THEM MONEY.
entries.display: How Cyrus, king of the Persians, delivered the Jews out of Babylon, and suffered them to return to their own country, and to build their temple; for which work he gave them money.

entries.label: II
entries.original: HOW, UPON THE DEATH OF CYRUS, THE JEWS WERE HINDERED IN BUILDING OF THE TEMPLE BY THE CUTHEANS, AND THE NEIGHBOURING GOVERNORS; AND HOW CAMBYSES INTIRELY FORBADE THE JEWS TO DO ANY SUCH THING.
entries.display: How, upon the death of Cyrus, the Jews were hindered in building of the temple by the Cutheans, and the neighbouring governors; and how Cambyses intirely forbade the Jews to do any such thing.

entries.label: III
entries.original: HOW, AFTER THE DEATH OF CAMBYSES, AND THE SLAUGHTER OF THE MAGI, BUT UNDER THE REIGN OF DARIUS, ZOROBABEL WAS SUPERIOR TO THE REST IN THE SOLUTION OF PROBLEMS, AND THEREBY OBTAINED THIS FAVOUR OF THE KING, THAT THE TEMPLE SHOULD BE BUILT.
entries.display: How, after the death of Cambyses, and the slaughter of the magi, but under the reign of Darius, Zorobabel was superior to the rest in the solution of problems, and thereby obtained this favour of the king, that the temple should be built.

entries.label: IV
entries.original: HOW THE TEMPLE WAS BUILT, WHILE THE CUTHEANS ENDEAVOURED IN VAIN TO OBSTRUCT THE WORK.
entries.display: How the temple was built, while the Cutheans endeavoured in vain to obstruct the work.

entries.label: V
entries.original: HOW XERXES, THE SON OF DARIUS, WAS WELL-DISPOSED TO THE JEWS; AS ALSO CONCERNING ESDRAS AND NEHEMIAH.
entries.display: How Xerxes, the son of Darius, was well-disposed to the Jews; as also concerning Esdras and Nehemiah.

entries.label: VI
entries.original: CONCERNING ESTHER, AND MORDECAI, AND HAMAN; AND HOW, IN THE REIGN OF ARTAXERXES, THE WHOLE NATION OF THE JEWS WAS IN DANGER OF PERISHING.
entries.display: Concerning Esther, and Mordecai, and Haman; and how, in the reign of Artaxerxes, the whole nation of the Jews was in danger of perishing.

entries.label: VII
entries.original: HOW JOHN SLEW HIS BROTHER JESUS IN THE TEMPLE; AND HOW BAGOSES OFFERED MANY INJURIES TO THE JEWS; AND WHAT SANBALLAT DID.
entries.display: How John slew his brother Jesus in the temple; and how Bagoses offered many injuries to the Jews; and what Sanballat did.

entries.label: VIII
entries.original: CONCERNING SANBALLAT AND MANASSEH, AND THE TEMPLE WHICH THEY BUILT ON MOUNT GERIZZIM; AS ALSO HOW ALEXANDER MADE HIS ENTRY INTO THE CITY JERUSALEM; AND WHAT BENEFITS HE BESTOWED ON THE JEWS.
entries.display: Concerning Sanballat and Manasseh, and the temple which they built on Mount Gerizzim; as also how Alexander made his entry into the city Jerusalem; and what benefits he bestowed on the Jews.

entries.label: I
entries.original: HOW PTOLEMY, THE SON OF LAGUS, TOOK JERUSALEM AND JUDEA BY DECEIT AND TREACHERY, AND CARRIED MANY OF THE JEWS THENCE, AND PLANTED THEM IN EGYPT.
entries.display: How Ptolemy, the son of Lagus, took Jerusalem and Judea by deceit and treachery, and carried many of the Jews thence, and planted them in Egypt.

entries.label: II
entries.original: HOW PTOLEMY PHILADELPHUS PROCURED THE LAWS OF THE JEWS TO BE TRANSLATED INTO THE GREEK TONGUE; AND SET MANY CAPTIVES FREE; AND DEDICATED MANY GIFTS TO GOD.
entries.display: How Ptolemy Philadelphus procured the laws of the Jews to be translated into the Greek tongue; and set many captives free; and dedicated many gifts to God.

entries.label: III
entries.original: HOW THE KINGS OF ASIA HONOURED THE NATION OF THE JEWS, AND MADE THEM CITIZENS OF THOSE CITIES WHICH THEY BUILT.
entries.display: How the kings of Asia honoured the nation of the Jews, and made them citizens of those cities which they built.

entries.label: IV
entries.original: HOW ANTIOCHUS MADE A LEAGUE WITH PTOLEMY; AND HOW ONIAS PROVOKED PTOLEMY EUERGETES TO ANGER; AND HOW JOSEPH BROUGHT ALL THINGS RIGHT AGAIN, AND ENTERED INTO A FRIENDSHIP WITH HIM; AND WHAT OTHER THINGS WERE DONE BY JOSEPH, AND HIS SON HYRCANUS.
entries.display: How Antiochus made a league with Ptolemy; and how Onias provoked Ptolemy Euergetes to anger; and how Joseph brought all things right again, and entered into a friendship with him; and what other things were done by Joseph, and his son Hyrcanus.

entries.label: V
entries.original: HOW, UPON THE QUARRELS OF THE JEWS ONE AGAINST ANOTHER ABOUT THE HIGH-PRIESTHOOD, ANTIOCHUS MADE AN EXPEDITION AGAINST JERUSALEM, TOOK THE CITY, AND PILLAGED THE TEMPLE, AND DISTRESSED THE JEWS: AS ALSO, HOW MANY OF THE JEWS FORSOOK THE LAWS OF THEIR COUNTRY; AND HOW THE SAMARITANS FOLLOWED THE CUSTOMS OF THE GREEKS, AND NAMED THEIR TEMPLE AT MOUNT GERIZZIM, THE TEMPLE OF JUPITER HELLENIUS.
entries.display: How, upon the quarrels of the Jews one against another about the high-priesthood, Antiochus made an expedition against Jerusalem, took the city, and pillaged the temple, and distressed the Jews: as also, how many of the Jews forsook the laws of their country; and how the Samaritans followed the customs of the Greeks, and named their temple at Mount Gerizzim, the temple of Jupiter Hellenius.

entries.label: VI
entries.original: HOW, UPON ANTIOCHUS'S PROHIBITION TO THE JEWS TO MAKE USE OF THE LAWS OF THEIR COUNTRY, MATTATHIAS, THE SON OF ASAMONEUS, ALONE DESPISED THE KING, AND OVERCAME THE GENERALS OF ANTIOCHUS'S ARMY: AS ALSO CONCERNING THE DEATH OF MATTATHIAS, AND THE SUCCESSION OF JUDAS.
entries.display: How, upon Antiochus's prohibition to the Jews to make use of the laws of their country, Mattathias, the son of Asamoneus, alone despised the king, and overcame the generals of Antiochus's army: as also concerning the death of Mattathias, and the succession of Judas.

entries.label: VII
entries.original: HOW JUDAS OVERTHREW THE FORCES OF APOLLONIUS AND SERON, AND KILLED THE GENERALS OF THEIR ARMIES THEMSELVES; AND HOW WHEN, A LITTLE WHILE AFTERWARD, LYSIAS AND GORGIAS WERE BEATEN, HE WENT UP TO JERUSALEM, AND PURIFIED THE TEMPLE.
entries.display: How Judas overthrew the forces of Apollonius and Seron, and killed the generals of their armies themselves; and how when, a little while afterward, Lysias and Gorgias were beaten, he went up to Jerusalem, and purified the temple.

entries.label: VIII
entries.original: HOW JUDAS SUBDUED THE NATIONS ROUND ABOUT; AND HOW SIMON BEAT THE PEOPLE OF TYRE AND PTOLEMAIS; AND HOW JUDAS OVERTHREW TIMOTHEUS, AND FORCED HIM TO FLY AWAY, AND DID MANY OTHER THINGS AFTER JOSEPH AND AZARIAS HAD BEEN BEATEN.
entries.display: How Judas subdued the nations round about; and how Simon beat the people of Tyre and Ptolemais; and how Judas overthrew Timotheus, and forced him to fly away, and did many other things after Joseph and Azarias had been beaten.

entries.label: IX
entries.original: CONCERNING THE DEATH OF ANTIOCHUS EPIPHANES; HOW ANTIOCHUS EUPATOR FOUGHT AGAINST JUDAS, AND BESIEGED HIM IN THE TEMPLE, AND AFTERWARDS MADE PEACE WITH HIM, AND DEPARTED. OF ALCIMUS AND ONIAS.
entries.display: Concerning the death of Antiochus Epiphanes; how Antiochus Eupator fought against Judas, and besieged him in the temple, and afterwards made peace with him, and departed. Of Alcimus and Onias.

entries.label: X
entries.original: HOW BACCHIDES, THE GENERAL OF DEMETRIUS'S ARMY, MADE AN EXPEDITION AGAINST JUDEA, AND RETURNED WITHOUT SUCCESS; AND HOW NICANOR WAS SENT A LITTLE AFTERWARD AGAINST JUDAS, AND PERISHED, TOGETHER WITH HIS ARMY; AS ALSO CONCERNING THE DEATH OF ALCIMUS, AND THE SUCCESSION OF JUDAS.
entries.display: How Bacchides, the general of Demetrius's army, made an expedition against Judea, and returned without success; and how Nicanor was sent a little afterward against Judas, and perished, together with his army; as also concerning the death of Alcimus, and the succession of Judas.

entries.label: XI
entries.original: THAT BACCHIDES WAS AGAIN SENT OUT AGAINST JUDAS; AND HOW JUDAS FELL AS HE WAS COURAGEOUSLY FIGHTING.
entries.display: That Bacchides was again sent out against Judas; and how Judas fell as he was courageously fighting.

entries.label: I
entries.original: HOW JONATHAN TOOK THE GOVERNMENT AFTER HIS BROTHER JUDAS; AND HOW HE, TOGETHER WITH HIS BROTHER SIMON, WAGED WAR AGAINST BACCHIDES.
entries.display: How Jonathan took the government after his brother Judas; and how he, together with his brother Simon, waged war against Bacchides.

entries.label: II
entries.original: HOW ALEXANDER [BALA], IN HIS WAR WITH DEMETRIUS, GRANTED JONATHAN MANY ADVANTAGES, AND APPOINTED HIM TO BE HIGH-PRIEST, AND PERSUADED HIM TO ASSIST HIM, ALTHOUGH DEMETRIUS PROMISED HIM GREATER ADVANTAGES ON THE OTHER SIDE. CONCERNING THE DEATH OF DEMETRIUS.
entries.display: How Alexander [Bala], in his war with Demetrius, granted Jonathan many advantages, and appointed him to be high-priest, and persuaded him to assist him, although Demetrius promised him greater advantages on the other side. Concerning the death of Demetrius.

entries.label: III
entries.original: THE FRIENDSHIP THAT WAS BETWEEN ONIAS AND PTOLEMY PHILOMETOR; AND HOW ONIAS BUILT A TEMPLE IN EGYPT LIKE TO THAT AT JERUSALEM.
entries.display: The friendship that was between Onias and Ptolemy Philometor; and how Onias built a temple in Egypt like to that at Jerusalem.

entries.label: IV
entries.original: HOW ALEXANDER HONOURED JONATHAN AFTER AN EXTRAORDINARY MANNER; AND HOW DEMETRIUS, THE SON OF DEMETRIUS, OVERCAME ALEXANDER, AND MADE A LEAGUE OF FRIENDSHIP WITH JONATHAN.
entries.display: How Alexander honoured Jonathan after an extraordinary manner; and how Demetrius, the son of Demetrius, overcame Alexander, and made a league of friendship with Jonathan.

entries.label: V
entries.original: HOW TRYPHO, AFTER HE HAD BEATEN DEMETRIUS, DELIVERED THE KINGDOM TO ANTIOCHUS, THE SON OF ALEXANDER, AND GAINED JONATHAN FOR HIS ASSISTANT; AND CONCERNING THE ACTIONS AND EMBASSIES OF JONATHAN.
entries.display: How Trypho, after he had beaten Demetrius, delivered the kingdom to Antiochus, the son of Alexander, and gained Jonathan for his assistant; and concerning the actions and embassies of Jonathan.

entries.label: VI
entries.original: HOW JONATHAN WAS SLAIN BY TREACHERY; AND HOW THEREUPON THE JEWS MADE SIMON THEIR GENERAL AND HIGH-PRIEST: WHAT COURAGEOUS ACTIONS HE ALSO PERFORMED, ESPECIALLY AGAINST TRYPHO.
entries.display: How Jonathan was slain by treachery; and how thereupon the Jews made Simon their general and high-priest: what courageous actions he also performed, especially against Trypho.

entries.label: VII
entries.original: HOW SIMON CONFEDERATED HIMSELF WITH ANTIOCHUS PIUS, AND MADE WAR AGAINST TRYPHO, AND, A LITTLE AFTERWARDS, AGAINST CENDEBEUS, THE GENERAL OF ANTIOCHUS'S ARMY: AS ALSO HOW SIMON WAS MURDERED BY HIS SON-IN-LAW, PTOLEMY, AND THAT BY TREACHERY.
entries.display: How Simon confederated himself with Antiochus Pius, and made war against Trypho, and, a little afterwards, against Cendebeus, the general of Antiochus's army: as also how Simon was murdered by his son-in-law, Ptolemy, and that by treachery.

entries.label: VIII
entries.original: HYRCANUS RECEIVES THE HIGH-PRIESTHOOD, AND EJECTS PTOLEMY OUT OF THE COUNTRY. ANTIOCHUS MAKES WAR AGAINST HYRCANUS, AND AFTERWARDS MAKES A LEAGUE WITH HIM.
entries.display: Hyrcanus receives the high-priesthood, and ejects Ptolemy out of the country. Antiochus makes war against Hyrcanus, and afterwards makes a league with him.

entries.label: IX
entries.original: HOW, AFTER THE DEATH OF ANTIOCHUS, HYRCANUS MADE AN EXPEDITION AGAINST SYRIA, AND MADE A LEAGUE WITH THE ROMANS. CONCERNING THE DEATH OF KING DEMETRIUS AND ALEXANDER.
entries.display: How, after the death of Antiochus, Hyrcanus made an expedition against Syria, and made a league with the Romans. Concerning the death of king Demetrius and Alexander.

entries.label: X
entries.original: HOW, UPON THE QUARREL BETWEEN ANTIOCHUS GRYPUS AND ANTIOCHUS CYZICENUS, ABOUT THE KINGDOM, HYRCANUS TOOK SAMARIA, AND UTTERLY DEMOLISHED IT; AND HOW HYRCANUS JOINED HIMSELF TO THE SECT OF THE SADDUCEES, AND LEFT THAT OF THE PHARISEES.
entries.display: How, upon the quarrel between Antiochus Grypus and Antiochus Cyzicenus, about the kingdom, Hyrcanus took Samaria, and utterly demolished it; and how Hyrcanus joined himself to the sect of the Sadducees, and left that of the Pharisees.

entries.label: XI
entries.original: HOW ARISTOBULUS, WHEN HE HAD TAKEN THE GOVERNMENT, FIRST OF ALL PUT A DIADEM ON HIS HEAD, AND WAS MOST BARBAROUSLY CRUEL TO HIS MOTHER AND HIS BRETHREN; AND HOW, AFTER HE HAD SLAIN ANTIGONUS, HE HIMSELF DIED.
entries.display: How Aristobulus, when he had taken the government, first of all put a diadem on his head, and was most barbarously cruel to his mother and his brethren; and how, after he had slain Antigonus, he himself died.

entries.label: XII
entries.original: HOW ALEXANDER, WHEN HE HAD TAKEN THE GOVERNMENT, MADE AN EXPEDITION AGAINST PTOLEMAIS, AND THEN RAISED THE SIEGE, OUT OF FEAR OF PTOLEMY LATHYRUS; AND HOW PTOLEMY MADE WAR AGAINST HIM, BECAUSE HE HAD SENT TO CLEOPATRA TO PERSUADE HER TO MAKE WAR AGAINST PTOLEMY, AND YET PRETENDED TO BE IN FRIENDSHIP WITH HIM, WHEN HE WENT TO BEAT THE JEWS IN BATTLE.
entries.display: How Alexander, when he had taken the government, made an expedition against Ptolemais, and then raised the siege, out of fear of Ptolemy Lathyrus; and how Ptolemy made war against him, because he had sent to Cleopatra to persuade her to make war against Ptolemy, and yet pretended to be in friendship with him, when he went to beat the Jews in battle.

entries.label: XIII
entries.original: HOW ALEXANDER, UPON THE LEAGUE OF MUTUAL DEFENCE WHICH CLEOPATRA HAD AGREED WITH HIM, MADE AN EXPEDITION AGAINST CELESYRIA, AND UTTERLY OVERTHREW THE CITY OF GAZA; AND HOW HE SLEW MANY TEN THOUSANDS OF JEWS THAT HAD REBELLED AGAINST HIM; ALSO CONCERNING ANTIOCHUS GRYPUS, SELEUCUS, ANTIOCHUS CYZICENUS, AND ANTIOCHUS PIUS, AND OTHERS.
entries.display: How Alexander, upon the league of mutual defence which Cleopatra had agreed with him, made an expedition against Celesyria, and utterly overthrew the city of Gaza; and how he slew many ten thousands of Jews that had rebelled against him; also concerning Antiochus Grypus, Seleucus, Antiochus Cyzicenus, and Antiochus Pius, and others.

entries.label: XIV
entries.original: HOW DEMETRIUS EUCERUS OVERCAME ALEXANDER, AND YET, IN A LITTLE TIME, RETIRED OUT OF THE COUNTRY FOR FEAR OF THE JEWS; AS ALSO HOW ALEXANDER SLEW MANY OF THE JEWS, AND THEREBY GOT CLEAR OF HIS TROUBLES. CONCERNING THE DEATH OF DEMETRIUS.
entries.display: How Demetrius Eucerus overcame Alexander, and yet, in a little time, retired out of the country for fear of the Jews; as also how Alexander slew many of the Jews, and thereby got clear of his troubles. Concerning the death of Demetrius.

entries.label: XV
entries.original: HOW ANTIOCHUS, WHO WAS CALLED DIONYSUS, AND AFTER HIM ARETAS, MADE EXPEDITIONS INTO JUDEA; AS ALSO HOW ALEXANDER TOOK MANY CITIES, AND THEN RETURNED TO JERUSALEM, AND, AFTER A SICKNESS OF THREE YEARS, DIED: AND WHAT COUNSEL HE GAVE TO ALEXANDRA.
entries.display: How Antiochus, who was called Dionysus, and after him Aretas, made expeditions into Judea; as also how Alexander took many cities, and then returned to Jerusalem, and, after a sickness of three years, died: and what counsel he gave to Alexandra.

entries.label: XVI
entries.original: HOW ALEXANDRA, BY GAINING THE GOOD-WILL OF THE PHARISEES, RETAINED THE KINGDOM NINE YEARS, AND THEN, HAVING DONE MANY GLORIOUS ACTIONS, DIED.
entries.display: How Alexandra, by gaining the good-will of the Pharisees, retained the kingdom nine years, and then, having done many glorious actions, died.

entries.label: I
entries.original: THE WAR BETWEEN ARISTOBULUS AND HYRCANUS ABOUT THE KINGDOM; AND HOW THEY MADE AN AGREEMENT THAT ARISTOBULUS SHOULD BE KING, AND HYRCANUS LIVE A PRIVATE LIFE: AS ALSO HOW HYRCANUS, A LITTLE AFTERWARDS, WAS PERSUADED BY ANTIPATER TO FLY TO ARETAS.
entries.display: The war between Aristobulus and Hyrcanus about the kingdom; and how they made an agreement that Aristobulus should be king, and Hyrcanus live a private life: as also how Hyrcanus, a little afterwards, was persuaded by Antipater to fly to Aretas.

entries.label: II
entries.original: HOW ARETAS AND HYRCANUS MADE AN EXPEDITION AGAINST ARISTOBULUS, AND BESIEGED JERUSALEM; AND HOW SCAURUS THE ROMAN GENERAL RAISED THE SIEGE. CONCERNING THE DEATH OF ONIAS.
entries.display: How Aretas and Hyrcanus made an expedition against Aristobulus, and besieged Jerusalem; and how Scaurus the Roman general raised the siege. Concerning the death of Onias.

entries.label: III
entries.original: HOW ARISTOBULUS AND HYRCANUS CAME TO POMPEY, IN ORDER TO ARGUE WHO OUGHT TO HAVE THE KINGDOM; AND HOW, UPON THE FLIGHT OF ARISTOBULUS TO THE FORTRESS ALEXANDRIUM, POMPEY LED HIS ARMY AGAINST HIM, AND ORDERED HIM TO DELIVER UP THE FORTRESSES WHEREOF HE WAS POSSESSED.
entries.display: How Aristobulus and Hyrcanus came to Pompey, in order to argue who ought to have the kingdom; and how, upon the flight of Aristobulus to the fortress Alexandrium, Pompey led his army against him, and ordered him to deliver up the fortresses whereof he was possessed.

entries.label: IV
entries.original: HOW POMPEY, WHEN THE CITIZENS OF JERUSALEM SHUT THEIR GATES AGAINST HIM, BESIEGED THE CITY, AND TOOK IT BY FORCE; AS ALSO WHAT OTHER THINGS HE DID IN JUDEA.
entries.display: How Pompey, when the citizens of Jerusalem shut their gates against him, besieged the city, and took it by force; as also what other things he did in Judea.

entries.label: V
entries.original: HOW SCAURUS MADE A LEAGUE OF MUTUAL ASSISTANCE WITH ARETAS; AND WHAT GABINIUS DID IN JUDEA, AFTER HE HAD CONQUERED ALEXANDER, THE SON OF ARISTOBULUS.
entries.display: How Scaurus made a league of mutual assistance with Aretas; and what Gabinius did in Judea, after he had conquered Alexander, the son of Aristobulus.

entries.label: VI
entries.original: HOW GABINIUS CAUGHT ARISTOBULUS AFTER HE HAD FLED FROM ROME, AND SENT HIM BACK TO ROME AGAIN; AND HOW THE SAME GABINIUS, AS HE RETURNED OUT OF EGYPT, OVERCAME ALEXANDER AND THE NABATEANS IN BATTLE.
entries.display: How Gabinius caught Aristobulus after he had fled from Rome, and sent him back to Rome again; and how the same Gabinius, as he returned out of Egypt, overcame Alexander and the Nabateans in battle.

entries.label: VII
entries.original: HOW CRASSUS CAME INTO JUDEA, AND PILLAGED THE TEMPLE; AND THEN MARCHED AGAINST THE PARTHIANS, AND PERISHED, WITH HIS ARMY. ALSO HOW CASSIUS OBTAINED SYRIA, AND PUT A STOP TO THE PARTHIANS, AND THEN WENT UP TO JUDEA.
entries.display: How Crassus came into Judea, and pillaged the temple; and then marched against the Parthians, and perished, with his army. Also how Cassius obtained Syria, and put a stop to the Parthians, and then went up to Judea.

entries.label: VIII
entries.original: THE JEWS BECOME CONFEDERATES WITH CÆSAR WHEN HE FOUGHT AGAINST EGYPT. THE GLORIOUS ACTIONS OF ANTIPATER, AND HIS FRIENDSHIP WITH CÆSAR. THE HONOURS WHICH THE JEWS RECEIVED FROM THE ROMANS AND ATHENIANS.
entries.display: The Jews become confederates with Cæsar when he fought against Egypt. The glorious actions of Antipater, and his friendship with Cæsar. The honours which the Jews received from the Romans and Athenians.

entries.label: IX
entries.original: HOW ANTIPATER COMMITTED THE CARE OF GALILEE TO HEROD, AND THAT OF JERUSALEM TO PHASAELUS; AS ALSO, HOW HEROD, UPON THE JEWS' ENVY AT ANTIPATER, WAS ACCUSED BEFORE HYRCANUS.
entries.display: How Antipater committed the care of Galilee to Herod, and that of Jerusalem to Phasaelus; as also, how Herod, upon the Jews' envy at Antipater, was accused before Hyrcanus.

entries.label: X
entries.original: THE HONOURS THAT WERE PAID THE JEWS; AND THE LEAGUES THAT WERE MADE BY THE ROMANS, AND OTHER NATIONS, WITH THEM.
entries.display: The honours that were paid the Jews; and the leagues that were made by the Romans, and other nations, with them.

entries.label: XI
entries.original: HOW MARCUS† SUCCEEDED SEXTUS WHEN HE HAD BEEN SLAIN BY BASSUS'S TREACHERY, AND HOW, AFTER THE DEATH OF CÆSAR, CASSIUS CAME INTO SYRIA, AND DISTRESSED JUDEA; AS ALSO, HOW MALICHUS SLEW ANTIPATER, AND WAS HIMSELF SLAIN BY HEROD.
entries.display: How Marcus† succeeded Sextus when he had been slain by Bassus's treachery, and how, after the death of Cæsar, Cassius came into Syria, and distressed Judea; as also, how Malichus slew Antipater, and was himself slain by Herod.

entries.label: XII
entries.original: HEROD EJECTS ANTIGONUS, THE SON OF ARISTOBULUS, OUT OF JUDEA, AND GAINS THE FRIENDSHIP OF ANTONY, WHO WAS NOW COME INTO SYRIA, BY SENDING HIM MUCH MONEY; ON WHICH ACCOUNT HE WOULD NOT ADMIT OF THOSE THAT WOULD HAVE ACCUSED HEROD: AND WHAT IT WAS THAT ANTONY WROTE TO THE TYRIANS IN BEHALF OF THE JEWS.
entries.display: Herod ejects Antigonus, the son of Aristobulus, out of Judea, and gains the friendship of Antony, who was now come into Syria, by sending him much money; on which account he would not admit of those that would have accused Herod: and what it was that Antony wrote to the Tyrians in behalf of the Jews.

entries.label: XIII
entries.original: HOW ANTONY MADE HEROD AND PHASAELUS TETRARCHS, AFTER THEY HAD BEEN ACCUSED TO NO PURPOSE; AND HOW THE PARTHIANS, WHEN THEY BROUGHT ANTIGONUS INTO JUDEA, TOOK HYRCANUS AND PHASAELUS CAPTIVES. HEROD'S FLIGHT; AND WHAT AFFLICTIONS HYRCANUS AND PHASAELUS ENDURED.
entries.display: How Antony made Herod and Phasaelus tetrarchs, after they had been accused to no purpose; and how the Parthians, when they brought Antigonus into Judea, took Hyrcanus and Phasaelus captives. Herod's flight; and what afflictions Hyrcanus and Phasaelus endured.

entries.label: XIV
entries.original: HOW HEROD GOT AWAY FROM THE KING OF ARABIA, AND MADE HASTE TO GO INTO EGYPT, AND THENCE WENT IN HASTE ALSO TO ROME; AND HOW, BY PROMISING A GREAT DEAL OF MONEY TO ANTONY, HE OBTAINED OF THE SENATE AND OF CÆSAR TO BE MADE KING OF THE JEWS.
entries.display: How Herod got away from the king of Arabia, and made haste to go into Egypt, and thence went in haste also to Rome; and how, by promising a great deal of money to Antony, he obtained of the senate and of Cæsar to be made king of the Jews.

entries.label: XV
entries.original: HOW HEROD SAILED OUT OF ITALY TO JUDEA, AND FOUGHT WITH ANTIGONUS; AND WHAT OTHER THINGS HAPPENED IN JUDEA ABOUT THAT TIME.
entries.display: How Herod sailed out of Italy to Judea, and fought with Antigonus; and what other things happened in Judea about that time.

entries.label: XVI
entries.original: HOW HEROD, WHEN HE HAD MARRIED MARIAMNE, TOOK JERUSALEM, WITH THE ASSISTANCE OF SOSIUS, BY FORCE; AND HOW THE GOVERNMENT OF THE ASAMONEANS WAS PUT AN END TO.
entries.display: How Herod, when he had married Mariamne, took Jerusalem, with the assistance of Sosius, by force; and how the government of the Asamoneans was put an end to.

entries.label: I
entries.original: CONCERNING POLLIO AND SAMEAS. HEROD SLAYS THE PRINCIPAL OF ANTIGONUS'S FRIENDS, AND SPOILS THE CITY OF ITS WEALTH. ANTONY BEHEADS ANTIGONUS.
entries.display: Concerning Pollio and Sameas. Herod slays the principal of Antigonus's friends, and spoils the city of its wealth. Antony beheads Antigonus.

entries.label: II
entries.original: HOW HYRCANUS WAS SET AT LIBERTY BY THE PARTHIANS, AND RETURNED TO HEROD; AND WHAT ALEXANDRA DID WHEN SHE HEARD THAT ANANELUS WAS MADE HIGH-PRIEST.
entries.display: How Hyrcanus was set at liberty by the Parthians, and returned to Herod; and what Alexandra did when she heard that Ananelus was made high-priest.

entries.label: III
entries.original: HOW HEROD, UPON HIS MAKING ARISTOBULUS HIGH-PRIEST, TOOK CARE THAT HE SHOULD BE MURDERED IN A LITTLE TIME; AND WHAT APOLOGY HE MADE TO ANTONY ABOUT ARISTOBULUS: AS ALSO CONCERNING JOSEPH AND MARIAMNE.
entries.display: How Herod, upon his making Aristobulus high-priest, took care that he should be murdered in a little time; and what apology he made to Antony about Aristobulus: as also concerning Joseph and Mariamne.

entries.label: IV
entries.original: HOW CLEOPATRA, WHEN SHE HAD GOTTEN FROM ANTONY SOME PARTS OF JUDEA AND ARABIA, CAME INTO JUDEA; AND HOW HEROD GAVE HER MANY PRESENTS, AND CONDUCTED HER ON HER WAY BACK TO EGYPT.
entries.display: How Cleopatra, when she had gotten from Antony some parts of Judea and Arabia, came into Judea; and how Herod gave her many presents, and conducted her on her way back to Egypt.

entries.label: V
entries.original: HOW HEROD MADE WAR WITH THE KING OF ARABIA, AND AFTER THEY HAD FOUGHT MANY BATTLES, AT LENGTH CONQUERED HIM, AND WAS CHOSEN BY THE ARABS TO BE GOVERNOR OF THAT NATION; AS ALSO CONCERNING A GREAT EARTHQUAKE.
entries.display: How Herod made war with the king of Arabia, and after they had fought many battles, at length conquered him, and was chosen by the Arabs to be governor of that nation; as also concerning a great earthquake.

entries.label: VI
entries.original: HOW HEROD SLEW HYRCANUS, AND THEN HASTED AWAY TO CÆSAR, AND OBTAINED THE KINGDOM FROM HIM ALSO; AND HOW, A LITTLE TIME AFTERWARD, HE ENTERTAINED CÆSAR IN A MOST HONOURABLE MANNER.
entries.display: How Herod slew Hyrcanus, and then hasted away to Cæsar, and obtained the kingdom from him also; and how, a little time afterward, he entertained Cæsar in a most honourable manner.

entries.label: VII
entries.original: HOW HEROD SLEW SOHEMUS AND MARIAMNE, AND AFTERWARDS ALEXANDRA AND COSTOBARUS, AND HIS MOST INTIMATE FRIENDS, AND, AT LAST, THE SONS OF BABA ALSO.
entries.display: How Herod slew Sohemus and Mariamne, and afterwards Alexandra and Costobarus, and his most intimate friends, and, at last, the sons of Baba also.

entries.label: VIII
entries.original: HOW TEN MEN OF THE CITIZENS [OF JERUSALEM] MADE A CONSPIRACY AGAINST HEROD, FOR THE FOREIGN PRACTICES HE HAD INTRODUCED, WHICH WAS A TRANSGRESSION OF THE LAWS OF THEIR COUNTRY. CONCERNING THE BUILDING OF SEBASTE AND CÆSAREA, AND OTHER EDIFICES OF HEROD.
entries.display: How ten men of the citizens [of Jerusalem] made a conspiracy against Herod, for the foreign practices he had introduced, which was a transgression of the laws of their country. Concerning the building of Sebaste and Cæsarea, and other edifices of Herod.

entries.label: IX
entries.original: CONCERNING THE FAMINE THAT HAPPENED IN JUDEA AND SYRIA; AND HOW HEROD, AFTER HE HAD MARRIED ANOTHER WIFE, REBUILT CÆSAREA, AND OTHER GRECIAN CITIES.
entries.display: Concerning the famine that happened in Judea and Syria; and how Herod, after he had married another wife, rebuilt Cæsarea, and other Grecian cities.

entries.label: X
entries.original: HOW HEROD SENT HIS SONS TO ROME; HOW ALSO HE WAS ACCUSED BY ZENODORUS AND THE GADARENS, BUT WAS CLEARED OF WHAT THEY ACCUSED HIM OF, AND WITHAL GAINED TO HIMSELF THE GOOD-WILL OF CÆSAR. CONCERNING THE PHARISEES, THE ESSENS, AND MANAHEM.
entries.display: How Herod sent his sons to Rome; how also he was accused by Zenodorus and the Gadarens, but was cleared of what they accused him of, and withal gained to himself the good-will of Cæsar. Concerning the Pharisees, the Essens, and Manahem.

entries.label: XI
entries.original: HOW HEROD REBUILT THE TEMPLE, AND RAISED IT HIGHER, AND MADE IT MORE MAGNIFICENT THAN IT WAS BEFORE; AND ALSO CONCERNING THAT TOWER WHICH HE CALLED ANTONIA.
entries.display: How Herod rebuilt the temple, and raised it higher, and made it more magnificent than it was before; and also concerning that tower which he called Antonia.

entries.label: I
entries.original: A LAW OF HEROD'S ABOUT THIEVES. SALOME AND PHERORAS CALUMNIATE ALEXANDER AND ARISTOBULUS, UPON THEIR RETURN FROM ROME, FOR WHOM HEROD YET PROVIDES WIVES.
entries.display: A law of Herod's about thieves. Salome and Pheroras calumniate Alexander and Aristobulus, upon their return from Rome, for whom Herod yet provides wives.

entries.label: II
entries.original: HOW HEROD TWICE SAILED TO AGRIPPA; AND HOW, UPON THE COMPLAINT OF THE JEWS IN IONIA AGAINST THE GREEKS, AGRIPPA CONFIRMED THE LAWS OF THE JEWS TO THEM.
entries.display: How Herod twice sailed to Agrippa; and how, upon the complaint of the Jews in Ionia against the Greeks, Agrippa confirmed the laws of the Jews to them.

entries.label: III
entries.original: HOW GREAT DISTURBANCES AROSE IN HEROD'S FAMILY ON HIS PREFERRING ANTIPATER, HIS ELDEST SON, BEFORE THE REST, TILL ALEXANDER TOOK THAT INJURY VERY HEINOUSLY.
entries.display: How great disturbances arose in Herod's family on his preferring Antipater, his eldest son, before the rest, till Alexander took that injury very heinously.

entries.label: IV
entries.original: HOW, DURING ANTIPATER'S ABODE AT ROME, HEROD BROUGHT ALEXANDER AND ARISTOBULUS BEFORE CÆSAR, AND ACCUSED THEM. ALEXANDER'S DEFENCE OF HIMSELF BEFORE CÆSAR, AND RECONCILIATION TO HIS FATHER.
entries.display: How, during Antipater's abode at Rome, Herod brought Alexander and Aristobulus before Cæsar, and accused them. Alexander's defence of himself before Cæsar, and reconciliation to his father.

entries.label: V
entries.original: HOW HEROD CELEBRATED THE GAMES THAT WERE TO RETURN EVERY FIFTH YEAR, UPON THE BUILDING OF CÆSAREA; AND HOW HE BUILT AND ADORNED MANY OTHER PLACES AFTER A MAGNIFICENT MANNER; AND DID MANY OTHER ACTIONS GLORIOUSLY.
entries.display: How Herod celebrated the games that were to return every fifth year, upon the building of Cæsarea; and how he built and adorned many other places after a magnificent manner; and did many other actions gloriously.

entries.label: VI
entries.original: AN EMBASSAGE OF THE JEWS IN CYRENE AND ASIA TO CÆSAR CONCERNING THE COMPLAINTS THEY HAD TO MAKE AGAINST THE GREEKS; WITH COPIES OF THE EPISTLES WHICH CÆSAR AND AGRIPPA WROTE TO THE CITIES FOR THEM.
entries.display: An embassage of the Jews in Cyrene and Asia to Cæsar concerning the complaints they had to make against the Greeks; with copies of the epistles which Cæsar and Agrippa wrote to the cities for them.

entries.label: VII
entries.original: HOW, UPON HEROD'S GOING DOWN INTO DAVID'S SEPULCHRE, THE SEDITION IN HIS FAMILY GREATLY INCREASED.
entries.display: How, upon Herod's going down into David's sepulchre, the sedition in his family greatly increased.

entries.label: VIII
entries.original: HOW HEROD TOOK UP ALEXANDER, AND BOUND HIM; WHOM YET ARCHELAUS, KING OF CAPPADOCIA, RECONCILED TO HIS FATHER HEROD AGAIN.
entries.display: How Herod took up Alexander, and bound him; whom yet Archelaus, king of Cappadocia, reconciled to his father Herod again.

entries.label: IX
entries.original: CONCERNING THE REVOLT OF THE TRACHONITES; HOW SYLLEUS ACCUSED HEROD BEFORE CÆSAR; AND HOW HEROD, WHEN CÆSAR WAS ANGRY AT HIM, RESOLVED TO SEND NICOLAUS TO ROME.
entries.display: Concerning the revolt of the Trachonites; how Sylleus accused Herod before Cæsar; and how Herod, when Cæsar was angry at him, resolved to send Nicolaus to Rome.

entries.label: X
entries.original: HOW EURYCLES FALSELY ACCUSED HEROD'S SONS; AND HOW THEIR FATHER BOUND THEM, AND WROTE TO CÆSAR ABOUT THEM. OF SYLLEUS; AND HOW HE WAS ACCUSED BY NICOLAUS.
entries.display: How Eurycles falsely accused Herod's sons; and how their father bound them, and wrote to Cæsar about them. Of Sylleus; and how he was accused by Nicolaus.

entries.label: XI
entries.original: HOW HEROD, BY PERMISSION FROM CÆSAR, ACCUSED HIS SONS BEFORE AN ASSEMBLY OF JUDGES AT BERYTUS; AND WHAT TERO SUFFERED, FOR USING A BOUNDLESS AND MILITARY LIBERTY OF SPEECH. CONCERNING ALSO THE DEATH OF THE YOUNG MEN, AND THEIR BURIAL AT ALEXANDRIUM.
entries.display: How Herod, by permission from Cæsar, accused his sons before an assembly of judges at Berytus; and what Tero suffered, for using a boundless and military liberty of speech. Concerning also the death of the young men, and their burial at Alexandrium.

entries.label: I
entries.original: HOW ANTIPATER WAS HATED BY ALL THE NATION [OF THE JEWS] FOR THE SLAUGHTER OF HIS BRETHREN; AND HOW, FOR THAT REASON, HE GOT INTO PECULIAR FAVOUR WITH HIS FRIENDS AT ROME, BY GIVING THEM MANY PRESENTS; AS HE DID ALSO WITH SATURNINUS, THE PRESIDENT OF SYRIA, AND THE GOVERNORS WHO WERE UNDER HIM; AND CONCERNING HEROD'S WIVES AND CHILDREN.
entries.display: How Antipater was hated by all the nation [of the Jews] for the slaughter of his brethren; and how, for that reason, he got into peculiar favour with his friends at Rome, by giving them many presents; as he did also with Saturninus, the president of Syria, and the governors who were under him; and concerning Herod's wives and children.

entries.label: II
entries.original: CONCERNING ZAMARIS, THE BABYLONIAN JEW; CONCERNING THE PLOTS LAID BY ANTIPATER AGAINST HIS FATHER; AND SOMEWHAT ABOUT THE PHARISEES.
entries.display: Concerning Zamaris, the Babylonian Jew; concerning the plots laid by Antipater against his father; and somewhat about the Pharisees.

entries.label: III
entries.original: CONCERNING THE ENMITY BETWEEN HEROD AND PHERORAS; HOW HEROD SENT ANTIPATER TO CÆSAR; AND OF THE DEATH OF PHERORAS.
entries.display: Concerning the enmity between Herod and Pheroras; how Herod sent Antipater to Cæsar; and of the death of Pheroras.

entries.label: IV
entries.original: PHERORAS'S WIFE IS ACCUSED BY HIS FREED-MEN AS GUILTY OF POISONING HIM; AND HOW HEROD, UPON EXAMINING OF THE MATTER BY TORTURE, FOUND THE POISON; BUT SO THAT IT HAD BEEN PREPARED FOR HIMSELF BY HIS SON ANTIPATER; AND, UPON AN INQUIRY BY TORTURE, HE DISCOVERED THE DANGEROUS DESIGNS OF ANTIPATER.
entries.display: Pheroras's wife is accused by his freed-men as guilty of poisoning him; and how Herod, upon examining of the matter by torture, found the poison; but so that it had been prepared for himself by his son Antipater; and, upon an inquiry by torture, he discovered the dangerous designs of Antipater.

entries.label: V
entries.original: ANTIPATER'S NAVIGATION FROM ROME TO HIS FATHER; AND HOW HE WAS ACCUSED BY NICOLAUS OF DAMASCUS, AND CONDEMNED TO DIE BY HIS FATHER, AND BY QUINTILIUS VARUS, WHO WAS THEN PRESIDENT OF SYRIA; AND HOW HE WAS THEN BOUND TILL CÆSAR SHOULD BE INFORMED OF HIS CAUSE.
entries.display: Antipater's navigation from Rome to his father; and how he was accused by Nicolaus of Damascus, and condemned to die by his father, and by Quintilius Varus, who was then president of Syria; and how he was then bound till Cæsar should be informed of his cause.

entries.label: VI
