entries.original: CONCERNING THE DISEASE THAT HEROD FELL INTO, AND THE SEDITION WHICH THE JEWS RAISED THEREUPON; WITH THE PUNISHMENT OF THE SEDITIOUS.
entries.display: Concerning the disease that Herod fell into, and the sedition which the Jews raised thereupon; with the punishment of the seditious.

entries.label: VII
entries.original: HEROD HAS THOUGHTS OF KILLING HIMSELF WITH HIS OWN HAND; AND A LITTLE AFTERWARDS HE ORDERS ANTIPATER TO BE SLAIN.
entries.display: Herod has thoughts of killing himself with his own hand; and a little afterwards he orders Antipater to be slain.

entries.label: VIII
entries.original: CONCERNING HEROD'S DEATH, AND TESTAMENT, AND BURIAL.
entries.display: Concerning Herod's death, and testament, and burial.

entries.label: IX
entries.original: HOW THE PEOPLE RAISED A SEDITION AGAINST ARCHELAUS, AND HOW HE SAILED TO ROME.
entries.display: How the people raised a sedition against Archelaus, and how he sailed to Rome.

entries.label: X
entries.original: A SEDITION OF THE JEWS AGAINST SABINUS; AND HOW VARUS BROUGHT THE AUTHORS OF IT TO PUNISHMENT.
entries.display: A sedition of the Jews against Sabinus; and how Varus brought the authors of it to punishment.

entries.label: XI
entries.original: AN EMBASSAGE OF THE JEWS TO CÆSAR; AND HOW CÆSAR CONFIRMED HEROD'S TESTAMENT.
entries.display: An embassage of the Jews to Cæsar; and how Cæsar confirmed Herod's testament.

entries.label: XII
entries.original: CONCERNING A SPURIOUS ALEXANDER.
entries.display: Concerning a spurious Alexander.

entries.label: XIII
entries.original: HOW ARCHELAUS, UPON A SECOND ACCUSATION, WAS BANISHED TO VIENNA.
entries.display: How Archelaus, upon a second accusation, was banished to Vienna.

entries.label: I
entries.original: HOW CYRENIUS WAS SENT BY CÆSAR TO MAKE A TAXATION OF SYRIA AND JUDEA; AND HOW COPONIUS WAS SENT TO BE PROCURATOR OF JUDEA; CONCERNING JUDAS OF GALILEE, AND CONCERNING THE SECTS THAT WERE AMONG THE JEWS.
entries.display: How Cyrenius was sent by Cæsar to make a taxation of Syria and Judea; and how Coponius was sent to be procurator of Judea; concerning Judas of Galilee, and concerning the sects that were among the Jews.

entries.label: II
entries.original: HOW HEROD AND PHILIP BUILT SEVERAL CITIES IN HONOUR OF CÆSAR. CONCERNING THE SUCCESSION OF PRIESTS AND PROCURATORS; AS ALSO WHAT BEFEL PHRAATES, AND THE PARTHIANS.
entries.display: How Herod and Philip built several cities in honour of Cæsar. Concerning the succession of priests and procurators; as also what befel Phraates, and the Parthians.

entries.label: III
entries.original: SEDITION OF THE JEWS AGAINST PONTIUS PILATE; CONCERNING CHRIST, AND WHAT BEFEL PAULINA AND THE JEWS AT ROME.
entries.display: Sedition of the Jews against Pontius Pilate; concerning Christ, and what befel Paulina and the Jews at Rome.

entries.label: IV
entries.original: HOW THE SAMARITANS MADE A TUMULT, AND PILATE DESTROYED MANY OF THEM; HOW PILATE WAS ACCUSED, AND WHAT THINGS WERE DONE BY VITELLIUS RELATING TO THE JEWS AND THE PARTHIANS.
entries.display: How the Samaritans made a tumult, and Pilate destroyed many of them; how Pilate was accused, and what things were done by Vitellius relating to the Jews and the Parthians.

entries.label: V
entries.original: HEROD THE TETRARCH MAKES WAR WITH ARETAS, THE KING OF ARABIA, AND IS BEATEN BY HIM; AS ALSO CONCERNING THE DEATH OF JOHN THE BAPTIST. HOW VITELLIUS WENT UP TO JERUSALEM; TOGETHER WITH SOME ACCOUNT OF AGRIPPA, AND OF THE POSTERITY OF HEROD THE GREAT.
entries.display: Herod the tetrarch makes war with Aretas, the king of Arabia, and is beaten by him; as also concerning the death of John the Baptist. How Vitellius went up to Jerusalem; together with some account of Agrippa, and of the posterity of Herod the Great.

entries.label: VI
entries.original: OF THE NAVIGATION OF KING AGRIPPA TO ROME, TO TIBERIUS CÆSAR; AND HOW, UPON HIS BEING ACCUSED BY HIS OWN FREED-MAN, HE WAS BOUND; HOW ALSO HE WAS SET AT LIBERTY BY CAIUS AFTER TIBERIUS'S DEATH, AND WAS MADE KING OF THE TETRARCHY OF PHILIP.
entries.display: Of the navigation of king Agrippa to Rome, to Tiberius Cæsar; and how, upon his being accused by his own freed-man, he was bound; how also he was set at liberty by Caius after Tiberius's death, and was made king of the tetrarchy of Philip.

entries.label: VII
entries.original: HOW HEROD THE TETRARCH WAS BANISHED.
entries.display: How Herod the tetrarch was banished.

entries.label: VIII
entries.original: CONCERNING THE EMBASSAGE OF THE JEWS TO CAIUS;* AND HOW CAIUS SENT PETRONIUS INTO SYRIA, TO MAKE WAR AGAINST THE JEWS, UNLESS THEY WOULD RECEIVE HIS STATUE.
entries.display: Concerning the embassage of the Jews to Caius;* and how Caius sent Petronius into Syria, to make war against the Jews, unless they would receive his statue.

entries.label: IX
entries.original: WHAT BEFEL THE JEWS THAT WERE IN BABYLON ON OCCASION OF ASINEUS AND ANILEUS, TWO BRETHREN.
entries.display: What befel the Jews that were in Babylon on occasion of Asineus and Anileus, two brethren.

entries.label: I
entries.original: HOW CAIUS* WAS SLAIN BY CHEREA.
entries.display: How Caius* was slain by Cherea.

entries.label: II
entries.original: HOW THE SENATORS DETERMINED TO RESTORE THE DEMOCRACY; BUT THE SOLDIERS WERE FOR PRESERVING THE MONARCHY. CONCERNING THE SLAUGHTER OF CAIUS'S WIFE AND DAUGHTER. A CHARACTER OF CAIUS'S MORALS.
entries.display: How the senators determined to restore the democracy; but the soldiers were for preserving the monarchy. Concerning the slaughter of Caius's wife and daughter. A character of Caius's morals.

entries.label: III
entries.original: HOW CLAUDIUS WAS SEIZED UPON, AND BROUGHT OUT OF HIS HOUSE, AND BROUGHT TO THE CAMP; AND HOW THE SENATE SENT AN EMBASSAGE TO HIM.
entries.display: How Claudius was seized upon, and brought out of his house, and brought to the camp; and how the senate sent an embassage to him.

entries.label: IV
entries.original: WHAT THINGS KING AGRIPPA DID FOR CLAUDIUS; AND HOW CLAUDIUS, WHEN HE HAD TAKEN THE GOVERNMENT, COMMANDED THE MURDERERS OF CAIUS TO BE SLAIN.
entries.display: What things king Agrippa did for Claudius; and how Claudius, when he had taken the government, commanded the murderers of Caius to be slain.

entries.label: V
entries.original: HOW CLAUDIUS RESTORED TO AGRIPPA HIS GRANDFATHER'S KINGDOMS, AUGMENTED HIS DOMINIONS; AND HOW HE PUBLISHED AN EDICT IN BEHALF OF THE JEWS.
entries.display: How Claudius restored to Agrippa his grandfather's kingdoms, augmented his dominions; and how he published an edict in behalf of the Jews.

entries.label: VI
entries.original: WHAT THINGS WERE DONE BY AGRIPPA AT JERUSALEM WHEN HE WAS RETURNED BACK INTO JUDEA; AND WHAT IT WAS THAT PETRONIUS WROTE TO THE INHABITANTS OF DORIS, IN BEHALF OF THE JEWS.
entries.display: What things were done by Agrippa at Jerusalem when he was returned back into Judea; and what it was that Petronius wrote to the inhabitants of Doris, in behalf of the Jews.

entries.label: VII
entries.original: CONCERNING SILAS.—AND ON WHAT ACCOUNT IT WAS THAT KING AGRIPPA WAS ANGRY AT HIM. HOW AGRIPPA BEGAN TO ENCOMPASS JERUSALEM WITH A WALL; AND WHAT BENEFITS HE BESTOWED ON THE INHABITANTS OF BERYTUS.
entries.display: Concerning Silas.—And on what account it was that king Agrippa was angry at him. How Agrippa began to encompass Jerusalem with a wall; and what benefits he bestowed on the inhabitants of Berytus.

entries.label: VIII
entries.original: WHAT OTHER ACTS WERE DONE BY AGRIPPA UNTIL HIS DEATH; AND AFTER WHAT MANNER HE DIED.
entries.display: What other acts were done by Agrippa until his death; and after what manner he died.

entries.label: IX
entries.original: WHAT THINGS WERE DONE AFTER THE DEATH OF AGRIPPA; AND HOW CLAUDIUS, ON ACCOUNT OF THE YOUTH AND UNSKILFULNESS OF AGRIPPA, JUNIOR, SENT CUSPIUS FADUS TO BE PROCURATOR OF JUDEA, AND OF THE ENTIRE KINGDOM.
entries.display: What things were done after the death of Agrippa; and how Claudius, on account of the youth and unskilfulness of Agrippa, junior, sent Cuspius Fadus to be procurator of Judea, and of the entire kingdom.

entries.label: I
entries.original: A SEDITION OF THE PHILADELPHIANS AGAINST THE JEWS; AND ALSO CONCERNING THE VESTMENTS OF THE HIGH-PRIEST.
entries.display: A sedition of the Philadelphians against the Jews; and also concerning the vestments of the high-priest.

entries.label: II
entries.original: HOW HELENA, THE QUEEN OF ADIABENE, AND HER SON, IZATES, EMBRACED THE JEWISH RELIGION; AND HOW HELENA SUPPLIED THE POOR WITH CORN, WHEN THERE WAS A GREAT FAMINE AT JERUSALEM.
entries.display: How Helena, the queen of Adiabene, and her son, Izates, embraced the Jewish religion; and how Helena supplied the poor with corn, when there was a great famine at Jerusalem.

entries.label: III
entries.original: HOW ARTABANUS, THE KING OF PARTHIA, OUT OF FEAR OF THE SECRET CONTRIVANCES OF HIS SUBJECTS AGAINST HIM, WENT TO IZATES, AND WAS BY HIM REINSTATED IN HIS GOVERNMENT; AS ALSO HOW BARDANES, HIS SON, DENOUNCED WAR AGAINST IZATES.
entries.display: How Artabanus, the king of Parthia, out of fear of the secret contrivances of his subjects against him, went to Izates, and was by him reinstated in his government; as also how Bardanes, his son, denounced war against Izates.

entries.label: IV
entries.original: HOW IZATES WAS BETRAYED BY HIS OWN SUBJECTS, AND FOUGHT AGAINST BY THE ARABIANS; AND HOW IZATES, BY THE PROVIDENCE OF GOD, WAS DELIVERED OUT OF THEIR HANDS.
entries.display: How Izates was betrayed by his own subjects, and fought against by the Arabians; and how Izates, by the providence of God, was delivered out of their hands.

entries.label: V
entries.original: CONCERNING THEUDAS AND THE SONS OF JUDAS THE GALILEAN; AS ALSO WHAT CALAMITY FELL UPON THE JEWS ON THE DAY OF THE PASSOVER.
entries.display: Concerning Theudas and the sons of Judas the Galilean; as also what calamity fell upon the Jews on the day of the Passover.

entries.label: VI
entries.original: HOW THERE HAPPENED A QUARREL BETWEEN THE JEWS AND THE SAMARITANS; AND HOW CLAUDIUS PUT AN END TO THEIR DIFFERENCES.
entries.display: How there happened a quarrel between the Jews and the Samaritans; and how Claudius put an end to their differences.

entries.label: VII
entries.original: FELIX IS MADE PROCURATOR OF JUDEA; AS ALSO CONCERNING AGRIPPA, JUNIOR, AND HIS SISTERS.
entries.display: Felix is made procurator of Judea; as also concerning Agrippa, junior, and his sisters.

entries.label: VIII
entries.original: AFTER WHAT MANNER, UPON THE DEATH OF CLAUDIUS, NERO SUCCEEDED IN THE GOVERNMENT; AS ALSO WHAT BARBAROUS THINGS HE DID. CONCERNING THE ROBBERS, MURDERERS, AND IMPOSTORS, THAT AROSE WHILE FELIX AND FESTUS WERE PROCURATORS OF JUDEA.
entries.display: After what manner, upon the death of Claudius, Nero succeeded in the government; as also what barbarous things he did. Concerning the robbers, murderers, and impostors, that arose while Felix and Festus were procurators of Judea.

entries.label: IX
entries.original: CONCERNING ALBINUS, UNDER WHOSE PROCURATORSHIP THE JEWS WERE AGAIN AFFLICTED; AS ALSO WHAT EDIFICES WERE BUILT BY AGRIPPA.
entries.display: Concerning Albinus, under whose procuratorship the Jews were again afflicted; as also what edifices were built by Agrippa.

entries.label: X
entries.original: AN ENUMERATION OF THE HIGH-PRIESTS.
entries.display: An enumeration of the high-priests.

entries.label: XI
entries.original: CONCERNING FLORUS THE PROCURATOR, WHO NECESSITATED THE JEWS TO TAKE UP ARMS AGAINST THE ROMANS. THE CONCLUSION.
entries.display: Concerning Florus the procurator, who necessitated the Jews to take up arms against the Romans. The conclusion.
